articleTitle: A Data-Driven Forecast Model of Ionospheric Slant Total Electron Content Based on Decision Trees
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The variability of ionospheric plasma exhibits irregularity at the micro-scale, but at the macro-level, the variation of ionospheric electron density can be predicted. Accurate prediction of ionospheric electron density is of great significance in wireless communication, navigation, and space weather forecasting. In this paper, we develop a data-driven prediction model using decision tree methodology based on the global navigation satellite system (GNSS) observation data and solar activity index, which achieves a single-station forecast model for ionospheric slant total electron content (STEC) one hour in advance. The prediction results for station (35°N,114°E) show that the root mean square error (RMSE) of STEC prediction using this method is 0.32 TECU and 0.48 TECU for the next ten and twenty minutes, respectively. After incorporating the solar activity index and geomagnetic disturbance index into the prediction factors, the accuracy of the model increases by 9.53%. Our research results demonstrate that the data-driven decision tree model for short-term ionospheric STEC prediction has high accuracy and reliability. This method has potential application values in improving GNSS positioning and navigation accuracy, optimizing communication system performance, and enhancing the monitoring capability of ionospheric anomalous behavior.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Input-Apsorptive Bandstop Filter Using Coupled Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel dual-band absorptive bandstop filter (ABSF) has been proposed, which adds an absorption resistor to the dual-band bandstop filter to absorb the return loss in the stopbands. As a result, the minimum value of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> within the stopband is 12.36 dB, and the return loss S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> is less than 10 dB across the entire frequency range. The center frequency of the stopband and the absorption resistor has been derived through even/odd-mode analysis. The simulation and measurement results demonstrate good agreement, validating the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Thermal Coupling Analysis of Inverted-F Antenna Using HIE-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The hybrid implicit-explicit finite-difference time-domain (HIE-FDTD) method is proposed to analyze electromagnetic (EM) - thermal coupling effect of a dual-frequency inverted-F antenna in this paper. Firstly, HIE-FDTD method is employed to solve the EM field. Then, the EM power loss is served as the heat source in the heat transfer equation (HTE) to solve the thermal field. Compared with the traditional FDTD method, the HIE-FDTD method is weakly conditional stable and thus improves the computational efficiency obviously. It shows that simulated results of the HIE-FDTD method agree well with those calculated by using FDTD method, CST software and COMSOL software, but the computational efficiency of the HIE-FDTD method is much higher than that of conventional FDTD method, which validate the effectiveness of the HIE-FDTD method in the analysis of the EM-thermal coupling effect.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Simulation of a Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to simulate the influence of thermal deformation effect on the electromagnetic radiation performance of patch antenna, an electromagnetic-thermal-mechanical co-simulation method was proposed based on discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method, finite element time domain (FETD) method and finite element method (FEM). Maxwell equation is solved by DGTD method, heat conduction equation is solved by FETD method, and mechanical equation is solved by FEM method. The thermal simulation and mechanical simulation are coupled by thermal strain. Electromagnetic and thermal-mechanical simulations are coupled through structural deformation. The numerical results show that the radiation pattern will change if the thermal deformation effect of the patch antenna is taken into account.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Finite Element Thermal Solver with Large-scale Parallel Computing Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: MOOSE, an object-oriented parallel computing framework, has been universally utilized in developing numerical solver. In this work, a finite element method solver with large-scale parallel computing capability is developed based on the MOOSE framework for high-efficient and scalable thermal simulations. The performance of the developed numerical solver is evaluated through comparing the simulation results of a simplified AMD microprocessor with those obtained by the commercial software COMSOL. High consistence is achieved between the two groups of data, and the simulation time is greatly reduced through utilizing the inhouse simulator.

articleTitle: V2X Reliability Enhancement Through NLOS Links from IRS Random Scattering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) have demonstrated the potential of dynamic beam-steering which can aid NLOS-V2X communication by enhancing channel characteristics in 5G/6G networks. However, mobility of vehicles pose a practical challenge in fully harvesting the IRS scattering benefits for reliable V2X applications. This work aims to propose a comparatively low-cost and efficient method of random binary phase patterns for IRS which is combined with beam-steering patterns to scatter the incoming signals towards the targeted region on road. The diffusion of IRS reflected power is directly linked to the QoS performance criteria and the same is fullfiled through efficient manipulation of stochastic parameters of IRS random patterns. The achieved SNR gain is proportional to the update rate of the random pattern. The proposed scheme offers a trade-off between high channel capacity and enhanced reliability for NLOS-V2X links. The flexibility of using the benefits of beam-steering and controlled random scattering is key in achieving the desired performance for specific V2X communication scenarios. The scheme is applicable to a wide range of V2X frequencies, including 5.9GHz and mmWave frequencies.

articleTitle: Design of Quad-Element MIMO Antenna for mm Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper provides a printed patch with the benefits of low size and easy geometrical arrangement for fifth-generation (5G) 28 GHz communication networks. The patch antenna's radiator is defective with a circular slit for improved performance. The antenna has a wide working bandwidth while maintaining a good gain. Later, A four-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array is designed using this single antenna. It achieves The MIMO antenna also has an excellent envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and high diversity gain, indicating that it can be applied in a compact 5G smart device.

articleTitle: A Cross-range Scaling Method for ISAR Based on 2D MUSIC and WVD-Hough Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: For better understanding of the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image, scaling is a necessary step. However, the rotational angle between the radar and the noncooperative target is usually unknown, resulting in difficulty in the cross-range scaling. In this paper, the two-dimensional (2D) MUSIC is employed to extract isolated scattering centers of the target. Then, Wigner-Ville distribution combined with Hough transform (WVD-Hough transform) is utilized to estimate the chirp rates of the range cells in which the scattering centers locate. Finally, the cross-range scaling factor is determined and cross- range scaling of the ISAR image can be finished. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the cross-range scaling method.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Phased Array with 3:1 Octaves and 70° Scanning Range
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In existing reported phased arrays with ultra-wideband wide-angle scanning capability, the problem of small element spacing is widespread. To solve this problem, an ultra-wideband wide-angle scanning phased array is proposed in this paper. The proposed array element adopts vertical printed dipole fed by Marchand balun as radiating structures. To achieve wide-angle scanning capability, a wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) layer consisting of vertical rectangular patches is introduced and placed above the dipole patches. The spacing of the proposed element is 23.5mm (0.47λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">high</inf>, λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">high</inf> is the free-space wavelength at the highest operating frequency). The calculated results show that the proposed infinite array can scan to ±70°in the E/H-planes with an active VSWR below 3 within 2–6 GHz.

articleTitle: Human Behavior Recognition Using Micro-Doppler Signatures and 2D-CNN-LSTM Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: 2-dimensional convolutional neural network and long short-term memory (2D-CNN-LSTM) network and micro-Doppler signatures were used to recognize human behavior in this paper. First, frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar was used to acquire raw radar data. Then, the collected data were preprocessed to produce micro-Doppler signatures. The micro-Doppler signatures have temporal and spatial information. Hence, the 2D-CNN-LSTM network is proposed. The section of convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and a convolution long-short term memory one-dimension (ConvLSTM1D) layer were used to tackle temporal and spatial information. The long-short term memory (LSTM) layer was used to tackle temporal information. The 2D-CNN-LSTM network was experimentally found to be lightweight while achieving high accuracy.

Author Keywords: 2-dimensional convolutional neural networks and long short-term memory (2D-CNN-LSTM) network

articleTitle: Stable FDTD for the Time-Domain Wave Equation Resulted from Spherical Harmonic Expansions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the solution of the time-domain wave equation involved in spherical harmonic expansion (SHE) is revisited. The finite difference time domain (FDTD) method is a preferred choice for the second-order time-domain wave equation, while the traditional Courant–Friedrich–Levy (CFL) condition cannot be applied directly. It is found that the stability condition of the wave equation is associated with the degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. As the degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> increases, the upper limit of the time step declines. However, due to the strictness of the derived stability condition, we opted to verify it using non-uniform spatial sampling. Numerical results obtained from this approach provide justification for our analysis.

articleTitle: Fabrication-Constrained Conjugate Adjoint Gradient Inverse Design for Large-Scale Aperiodic Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a fabrication-constrained conjugate adjoint gradient inverse design method (FCAG-IDM) is proposed to optimize the structural parameters of large-scale aperiodic frequency selective surfaces (FSSs). A characteristic of the proposed FCAG-IDM is that it constrains the optimized variables in each iteration considering the fabrication precision. The main advantage of FCAG-IDM is to achieve a fast inverse design for the scattering performance of electrically large-scale structure by combining fast forward simulator, conjugate adjoint gradient descent, and fabrication-constraint. The proposed FCAG-IDM is validated by both numerical and experimental results.

articleTitle: Influence of Different Activation Functions on Neural Networks Computational RCS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to find out the most suitable activation function for neural networks regressive calculation of radar cross section (RCS). Different activation functions can give neural networks different feature of data processing. This paper chooses four different activation functions, and use them in same multilayers full connected neural networks to compare which one is more suitable for regressive computing RCS.

articleTitle: Spatially Adaptive Beamforming Based on Time-Modulated Programmable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper discusses a spatially adaptive beamforming method based on time-modulated programmable metasurface. The time-modulated array technology is combined with programmable metasurface and the multibeam characteristic of time-modulated array is utilized. Adaptive beamforming is realized by changing the opening and closing time of the channel switch of the metasurface unit, and the orientation pattern of the fundamental and harmonic components of the time-modulated array points to different directions in space under a specific modulation sequence.

articleTitle: Near-Field Distribution of VLF Scattering from a Finite-Length Conducting Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The present work focuses on the near-field scattering of a finite-length conducting cylinder immersed in the ionosphere below the very low frequency (VLF) range. In particular, the ionosphere has the characteristics of an anisotropic and non-reciprocal plasma. Using the integral equation (IE) approach and the method of moments (MoM), we develop a theoretical model for the VLF scattering in the near region. The contributions from the ordinary wave (O-wave) and extra-ordinary wave (E-wave) are added together to reflect total scattering. Numerical results show that there exists a “cohesion effect” along the direction of the geomagnetic field in the near zone of the scattered field. Additionally, the scattering to the E-wave is greater than that of the O-wave. Potentially, the theoretical formulations and the predicted phenomena would be helpful in exploring the ionosphere and outer space in the future.

articleTitle: Implantable Devices Based On Ultra-Wideband Miniaturized Implantable Antenna for Biotelemetry Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In non-uniform and lossy environments within the human body, detuning of implantable devices primarily occurs due to the peristaltic motion of organs (e.g., gastrointestinal tract) and periodic pulsation (e.g., heartbeat). Achieving a wide bandwidth to overcome detuning challenges is constrained by device specifications and the miniaturization of antennas. In this study, we developed a compact ultra-wideband(UWB) implantable antenna for biotelemetry applications. The relative bandwidth of the implantable antenna in this paper is 146% (0.52-3.3 GHz), operating within the Wireless Medical Telemetry Service (WMTS) and Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) frequency bands. To closely real human tissue, a three-layer homogeneous tissue phantom was constructed, and the antenna was integrated into the implantable medical devices (IMDs) composed of alumina. In the homogeneous phantom, the proposed antenna exhibited gains of -32.1 dBi, -22.1 dBi, and - 15.8 dBi at 915 MHz, 1.4 GHz, and 2.45 GHz, respectively. Simultaneously, the antenna meets the guidelines of IEEE C95.1-2005 and C95.1-1999.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Vortex Wave Array Based on Vivaldi Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The ultra wideband (UWB) vortex wave antenna carrying with orbital angular momentum (OAM) usually has low mode purity and complex structures. For this reason, the Vivaldi antennas with single gradient side-line are used as the array element to constructs an UWB OAM slot array with rotationally symmetric distribution and in-phase feeding. In this case, vortex waves with a relative bandwidth of 72% is achieved, and the average mode purity in band reaches 55%, while maintaining good directional pattern bandwidth. Obviously, this antenna structure can be used for ultra wideband communications in OAM modes.

articleTitle: Bistatic composite scattering modeling of sea surface and ship under different sea conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Electromagnetic scattering of target marine environments is of great significance in ocean remote sensing especially for high sea conditions. The coupled scattering field between the sea surface and the target becomes more complex for the bistatic case under high sea conditions. The bistatic composite scattering results between the target and the sea surface were presented using the modified four path method, and the impact of different sea conditions on the composite scattering was analyzed.

articleTitle: A Wideband GCPW-SIW Fed Slots Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A wideband GCPW-SIW fed slots antenna in millimeter wave band is designed in this paper. The structure is composed of four inclined slots which are placed on the one side of the SIW with three shorting vias and fed by GCPW transmission line. The simulated results show that the operating frequency band of the proposed antenna is 24.15-27.59GHz (13.23%), the antenna has a stable gain with a maximum value of 9.67dBi and high radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: A Tunable Absorber Based on Plasma Composite Material with Dual-Channel and Broadband Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a plasma hybrid material-based absorbing device combining broadband absorption with two-channel characteristics. Two materials with a similar absorption effect are selected, one is a tunable plasma, and the other is an optimized metasurface, which has achieved a good absorption effect. Indium tin oxide (ITO) films and foam layers with different resistivities form the basis for the upper and lower absorbing layers, while a tunable plasma tube array is located between the two absorbing layers. The simulation results show that the device can achieve 90% in the 1 to 20GHz frequency band or even more in three intervals: 2.2GHz to 4.2GHz, 9.8 to 12.3GHz, and 18 to 20GHz. Verifying that the device can realize the movement of the strong resonance point and the working frequency band by adjusting the variable parameters, which is of great use in high-power electromagnetic protection and radar stealth.

articleTitle: Ship Wake Detection in SAR Images based on Lightweight Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A new lightweight network for ship wake detection is proposed. Firstly, the wakes from moving ships are generated based on turbulent and Kelvin wake models. Then the Shooting and Bouncing Rays (SBR) fast imaging technology is used to calculate the SAR images of the ship wakes. The generated SAR images of ship wake are used as a data set for the lightweight parameter estimation network. Finally, the network is based on Deep Residual Network (ResNet). It uses the Non-local operations, Depthwise Separable Convolution (DSC) and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to improve the parameter estimation capability. In this way, the accurate estimation of ship velocity, ship length, width and draft depth in wake image can be realized. Experimental results show that the lightweight parameter estimation network can effectively estimate ship wake parameters. And the network is lighter than mainstream parameter estimation networks.

articleTitle: Research On Ship Small Target Detection In SAR Image Based On Improved YOLO-v7
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Small size, low resolution and difficult feature extraction of small targets in SAR images may cause missed and wrong detections. Aiming that this problem, this paper proposes an improved YOLO-v7 network to improve the detection accuracy. Due to lack of feature channel information, this paper introduces CA attention mechanism into the backbone feature extraction network to avoid loss of input feature position in the extraction process. Then, since the shallow semantic information contributes a lot to the model weight, this paper uses BiFPN structure for multi-scale feature fusion instead of the PANet in the YOLO-v7 network to increase residual links and strengthen the ability to express shallow features. By increasing the learning weight of each scale feature, the utilization rate of shallow features is improved. Comparisons base on RSDD-SAR ship detection data set shown that the proposed improved YOLO-v7 algorithm can effectively improve the recognition and detection ability of small ship targets, and the missed detection situation is obviously improved. The recognition accuracy rate reaches 91.54 %, which is 3.82 % higher than that of YOLO-v7 before improvement.

articleTitle: Spectrum Analysis of Triple Gaussian Pulse
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Gaussian pulse signal has a high coverage range in the frequency domain, which can effectively simulate the electromagnetic environment of equipment operation and stimulate susceptible phenomena. Previous researchers have developed a time-domain testing approach for EUT conducted susceptibility using Gaussian even pulse. We further studied the spectrum of triple Gaussian pulses and found that they have the characteristics of both frequency selection and maximum bandwidth decrease compared to Gaussian even pulse, which is expected to improve the accuracy and efficiency of their test results in conducted susceptibility time-domain test.

articleTitle: Broadband Circularly Polarized Hybrid Metasurface Antenna for Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A 38×38×4mm3 wideband circularly polarized (CP) antenna with Hybrid Metasurface (MTS) for wearable devices is proposed. The proposed antenna achieves CP radiation by cutting corners on a square microstrip patch. A hybrid MTS is placed above a square patch with cut corners, achieving broadband radiation performance. The working mechanism of hybrid MTS is analyzed by characteristic mode analysis (CMA). The simulated -10dB bandwidth is 40.1% (4.61-6.82 GHz) and the 3dB axial ratio bandwidth is 25.2% (5.16-6.55 GHz) with a peak gain of 8.1 dBi. In addition, the antenna has a front-to-back ratio of approximately 20 dB, which makes it suitable for wearable applications.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Diplexer with Low Insertion Loss and High Isolation Based on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) diplexer for 1.575/2.45/5.4GHz applications. Exceptional simulation results with low insertion loss are achieved by the LTCC diplexer through the implementation of a complementary structure that combines low-pass and high-pass filters. Specifically, it achieves insertion losses below 0.66dB, 0.72dB, and 0.5dB for applications at 1.575GHz, 2.45GHz, and 5.4GHz respectively. The size of the presented LTCC diplexer is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1.6}\times \mathbf{0.8}\times \mathbf{0.69}\ \mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>, which is significantly more compact when compared to previously reported LTCC diplexers. The LTCC circuit model and 3-D model are shown. The simulation proves modes are reliable.

articleTitle: Foldable Smartphone Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The development of full-screen smartphones has led to the continuous expansion of screen-to-body ratios. However, this metric alone cannot fully represent the pinnacle of smartphone design evolution. The advent of foldable smartphones has ushered in a new era in the cellular phone industry, giving rise to a more diverse and complex landscape of antenna designs. The performance of these antennas has a significant impact on the communication quality of foldable phones. In this paper, the coupling of two antennas of a foldable smartphone is investigated. Specifically, the traditional inverted-F antennas (IFA) and loop antennas are designed, which operate in the N78 (3.3 GHz-3.8 GHz) frequency band of the 5G spectrum. The proposed loop antennas exhibit outstanding isolation performance when the foldable smartphone is in the folded state without the need for external decoupling measures.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Identification of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles with Hardware Implementation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a deep learning identification of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) targets based on a two-stage loss function is proposed and implemented on Xilinx ZCU104 board. Through modeling and simulation, we obtain the scattering fields of UAVs, then it is converted into time-frequency image data set, and the custom two-stage loss function is used in the training process to obtain the optimal model. Finally., the model is transferred to the hardware platform to realize the classification process of the target by convolution neural network(CNN).

articleTitle: High Isolation RF MEMS Capacitive Shunt Switch for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents capacitive RF MEMS switch implemented on standard FBK process. High isolation of −33 dB and low insertion loss of −0.12 dB is achieved at the frequency band of 30 GHz. RF analysis is performed in CST microwave Studio whereas mechanical analysis is performed in Intellisuite. The design operates on low actuation voltage of 14.18 V to achieve desired displacement which makes it suitable for various application where power requirement is important. RF MEMS switches can be incorporated in various new generation application equipment where high linearity and wider bandwidth operation is required.

articleTitle: Efficient Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis from Multiple IBC Targets based on SDIE
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The electromagnetic characteristics of coated targets are of significant importance in various applications, from radar recognition to remote sensing. This work studies the efficient scattering analysis from multiple IBC (impedance boundary condition) targets. Due to the numerical stability and fast convergence behavior, the combined self-dual integral equation (C-SDIE) formulation is adopted for IBC surfaces. To improve the efficiency and reduce the complexity of the numerical study, each isolated unit in the multiple targets is treated individually, and the associated data structures are reused for identical targets. The coupling effects among two separated targets are evaluated through a transfer matrix. Moreover, an initial guess approach is presented to improve the convergence rate of the proposed method. Numerical examples are performed to demonstrate the correctness, accuracy and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Low-RCS Vivald Antenna Based on Formalized Water-based Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the out-of-band monostatic radar cross section (RCS) reduction of a traditional Vivaldi antenna is achieved by loading a water-based metasurface (WBM) consisting of a water column onto the surface of the antenna. The proposed antenna achieves average RCS reduction of -6 dB and -10 dB in (6–12 GHz) and (6–18 GHz) when the copolarized plane wave incident along the -z and -y axes, respectively. The working band of the proposed antenna is 2–6 GHz, in which the performance of the antenna is not affected by the WBM.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Omnidirectional High-Gain Printed Antenna Based on Continuous Transverse Stub and Dipole Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The Ku band is one of the most commonly used bands in satellite mobile communication systems. This paper introduces an omnidirectional high-gain printed antenna designed specifically for the Ku band. It is an antenna array composed of a continuous transverse stub (CTS) structure and a dipole formed by a pair of triangular patches. The antenna uses a printed structure for miniaturization and low profile, and is fed by a coplanar waveguide (CPW) and a coaxial line. Simulation results show that the antenna's bandwidth, defined as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S_{11}\vert < -10$</tex> dB, spans from 12.3 GHz to 15.5 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of 23%. The maximum gain of the antenna is 7.3 dBi at 13 GHz, and the roundness is less than 3.3 dB. The designed antenna effectively covers the most commonly used 12–14 GHz band within the Ku band, offering characteristics such as high gain, omnidirectional radiation, and miniaturization, which make it suitable to be applied to mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: Numerical Studies on Current Injection Methods of 3D Field Distribution of the Discontinuous Blowout Well
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: At present, the relief well is the most effective method to control blowout accidents where the accurate detection of the relative position between the relief well and the blowout well is the key to accurately imply the rescue operations. In the numerous methods, current injection method plays an irreplaceable role in blowout well detection. In this paper, a three-dimensional (3D) model of the discontinuous blowout well casing, a common scenario during well detection, is built and simulated with Finite Element Method (FEM). Both current flow and the corresponding magnetic field distribution are obtained. Moreover, the impact of the length of the fracture on the blowout well casing on the magnetic field magnitude is discussed. The results show that the longest fracture that can be detected by the magnetometer with a sensitivity of 2nT is 150m. The discontinuous model of blowout well casing proposed in this paper is of great theoretical value and lays a foundation for the research of the drilling work.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Input Deep Neural Network Model for Multi-variable Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To address the challenges of time-consuming and low precision in constructing a multi-variable electromagnetic problem model, a hierarchical input deep neural network model is proposed in this paper. Considering the importance of variables, batch processing is employed to effectively reduce the construction time and enhance the generalization ability of the network. Utilizing a wideband filter power divider as an example, compared with the traditional network models, the proposed model can reduce the maximum error by 27.58% and the running time by 26.24%, which validates the outperformance of the proposed model.

articleTitle: High-gain Dual-Polarized SIW Shared Aperture Magnetoelectric Dipoles Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain dual-polarized shared aperture magnetoelectric dipole (MED) antenna with substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) as feed network is proposed. The antenna element effective size is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.48 \lambda_{0} \times 0.48 \lambda_{0} \times 0.2 \lambda_{0}$</tex>. A bandwidth of 14% (36.4GHz-41.9GHz) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}11\vert < -10\text{dB}$</tex> can achieved. Antenna radiation pattern is superior, and it has unidirectional radiation. The peak gain of the antenna is 9.35dB, and the average gain is 8.65dBi. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> square array can be created by grouping the proposed MED antenna element. By adjusting the phase of each port, the four-beam radiation mode is realized. Based on the advantages of antenna radiation performance, it is conducive to processing and integration, and can be applied to wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Ka-Band Electromagnetic Tag Based on Space-Time Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a Ka-band metasurface-based electromagnetic (EM) tag employing binary frequency shift keying (BFSK) communication. Simulation and experimental results simultaneously show that the proposed EM tag can accurately transmit a piece of information containing ten symbols to the possible reader in a certain direction.

articleTitle: Study on SAR Image Simulation of Real Complex Ground Based on DEM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The actual complex ground consists of many types of terrains, and the scattering characteristics and electromagnetic (EM) parameters of different terrains are of great difference, which has a great influence on the SAR image simulation of the actual complex ground. In order to improve the accuracy and authenticity of SAR image simulation, this paper obtains the elevation information of the ground by DEM and adopts the DEM terrain division method based on terrain factor to divide the terrain. On this basis, the SBR is employed to establish the EM scattering model of the actual complex ground. Finally, the SAR image simulation of the actual complex ground is carried out based on the EM scattering model.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method for Impedance Matching Teardrop via Pads Based on TDR Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Teardrops is a way to prevent drill breakage in the Printed Circuit Board (PCB) design process, and it has a certain impedance matching effect. In this paper, we propose an optimization method based on (Time Domain Reflectometry) TDR simulation for impedance matching teardrop via pads, which achieves the effect of impedance matching by designing a track-type teardrop via pad. Simulation results show that using the default settings of a PCB drawing software, the impedance optimization of the via pads can be obtained at approximately 6.7%, while the best impedance optimization of the via pads can be achieved at approximately 36.7% using the optimization method in this paper. It is advantageous to design the teardrop via pads accurately, reducing the space taken up by the anti-pad and improving the system design margin.

articleTitle: Polarization Mismatch Analysis of the Randomly-Oriented RFID Tags Based on Monte Carlo Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper investigates the polarization mismatch influences from randomly-oriented tags to detection efficiencies for radio frequency identification (RFID) applications. The random numbers produced by Monte-Carlo method are used to define the orientation relationships between the different polarized reader and tag antennas, and further employed for the modeling and simulation analysis. Considering the polarization mismatch and environmental influences, the transmission losses over free space are calculated by the modified Friis equation. It is then used to compute the final detection efficiencies under different polarizations. The results are obtained under different transmitting powers and distances to give the guideline for the polarization reconfigurable reader antenna design.

articleTitle: Parallel Conformal Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method for Large-Scale Unmanned Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a high stable conformal technique based on finite difference time domain (FDTD) method for solving electromagnetic problem of curved metallic objects. The objective is to mitigate the staircase errors that are present in traditional FDTD algorithms when dealing with curved surfaces, as well as to reduce the computational time required for large-scale targets. The metallic conformal technique enhances accuracy by correcting the edge grid magnetic fields using Faraday's law. Furthermore, the parallel techniques has been adopted to accelerate the simulation process of FDTD computations by utilizing the MPI framework. The proposed method is applied to perform electromagnetic simulations of large-scale unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), solving for the field values at the corresponding observation points. The results demonstrate that this algorithm significantly improves computational accuracy and reduces the computation time for electromagnetic simulations.

articleTitle: Design of Microstrip Type Broadband Directional Coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A microstrip line broadband directional coupler is designed based on microstrip line theory. The bandwidth of the coupler is extended by using a cascade of multiple coupled lines. The isolation of the directional coupler is greatly improved by covering the microstrip line with a dielectric layer [1] and by loading the branching compensation capacitor to compensate for the odd-even mode phase velocity difference. Simulation results of ANSYS HFSS 2019 show that the return loss (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex>) is greater than 20 dB, the insertion loss (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex>) is less than 1.7 dB, the coupling degree (S31) is about −6dB(±0.8dB), the isolation degree (S41) is greater than 23.4dB, and the minimum directionality is greater than 17dB during 700 MHz-3700 MHz. The physical size of coupler is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$18\text{mm}\times 60\text{mm}$</tex>, which meets the design requirements of 6dB coupler.

articleTitle: Efficient Absorbing Boundary for LADI-FDTD Method*
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The finite difference time domain (FDTD) method is one of the most universal numerical methods for calculating electromagnetic problem. The conventional FDTD method was limited by the stability condition named CFL (Courant, Friedrichs and Lewy), and the calculation efficiency to be low. However, a method called leapfrog alternating direction implicit finite difference time domain (LADI-FDTD) was proposed, it was proved to be unconditional stability and have high computational efficiency. Moreover, the setting of absorbing boundary conditions plays an important role in FDTD. A new absorbing boundary based on Huygens surface combined with other boundary is applied to LADI-FDTD method, and its iterative equations were derived, it's obviously that is simple and easy to realize. Finally, the excellent absorbing performance of the boundary based on Huygens surface was verified by numerical calculation, which can significantly improve the efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: Reflection Characteristics of the VLF in Anisotropic Ionosphere By Hybrix Matrix Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose to analyze the reflection characteristics of VLF waves in anisotropic layered ionosphere by Hybrid Matrix Method. The reflection characteristics of VLF waves in anisotropic layered media are analyzed by calculating the coupling matrix c and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}$</tex> matrix from Maxwell's equation combined with the ionospheric permittivity tensor, and solving the reflection coefficient matrix in anisotropic layered media by H matrix, and comparing with the results of waveguide mode theory to clarify the correctness of the hybrid matrix method applied in VLF frequency band, which provides some reference for the study of VLF wave propagation characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of A Compact Broadband Microstrip Line Diplexer for VHF/UHF Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a compact broadband microstrip line diplexer for VHF/UHF frequency range is proposed. For miniaturization, lumped capacitance and curved microstrip lines acting as inductance are utilized to construct the diplexer. The two filters are located on two substrates and connected by an approximate coaxial line structure. The working bandwidth is 0.1 to 2.5 GHz. The transition bandwidth is from 0.902 to 0.967 GHZ. The final size of the combiner is just as small as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.07\lambda_{0}\times 0.16 \lambda_{0}= 1.3$</tex> GHz. Simulation results show the verification of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual Circularly Polarized Metasurface Antenna with Directional Coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband dual circularly polarized metasurface antenna. Through the combination of directional coupler and two-port microstrip metasurface antenna, the dual circularly polarized antenna can be realized. After simulation, the antenna has a VSWR ≤ 3 bandwidth from 3.17 GHz to 4 GHz, and has the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 12.4 % (3.17 ~ 3.59GHz) for two circularly polarized modes. And the antenna has the boresight radiation gains of more than 7.63 dBic.

articleTitle: A Compact Multi-layer Structure Based on Spiral Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons with High Efficiency of High-order Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A compact multi-layer structure based on spiral spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is presented, which achieved extreme miniaturization and high-efficient propagation of high-order modes of SSPPs. The cut-off frequencies of the fundamental mode and the first high-order mode are 1.9 GHz and 5.7 GHz, respectively. The lateral size reduction is 87% compared with the conventional structures with the same cut-off frequency. Both modes can be used for transmission lines. No asymptotic transition part is needed. Due to the surface wave characteristics, the proposed component can also be used as a permittivity sensor from 2.5 GHz to 5.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Circularly Polarized GPS Antenna Using Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A dual-band circularly polarized (CP) antenna using an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is proposed for global positioning system (GPS) applications in this paper. An AMC reflector is employed for improving the axial ratio (AR) performance while obtaining greater gain. The proposed antenna achieves right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) radiation with simulated gain of 5.7 dBi and 8.9 dBi in the GPS L2 (1.227 GHz) and L1 (1.575 GHz) bands, respectively. The simulated results show that -10 dB impedance bandwidths are 1.192-1.265 GHz and 1.534-1.648 GHz, 3 dB AR bandwidths are 1.223-1.238 GHz and 1.555-1.580 GHz, which is suitable for GPS.

articleTitle: Research on Amplitude Statistics from Targets Located Above Rough Ground Surface Covered by Vegetation Based on SBR-VRT Hybrid Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the SBR-VRT hybrid method is used to calculate the radar echoes of targets located above rough ground surface covered by vegetation. The maximum likelihood (ML) method is used to estimate the parameters of the clutter amplitude probability density function (PDF), and the K-S test is used to evaluate the goodness of fit between the clutter PDF and the different models PDF, and determine the best distribution fitting results. The features of ground clutter wave amplitude distribution under different conditions, including frequencies and angle of incidence, are studied, and the best distribution fitting results under different conditions are given. It can be found that the PDF of clutter amplitude at large incident angles under the L-band and S-band, is Log-normal distribution.

articleTitle: Wide-angle scanning gain stable millimeter wave leaky wave antenna based on ISGW
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a leaky wave antenna (LWA) based on integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW) and spoof surface plasmon polaritons transmission line(SSPPs TL). Due to the different transmission modes of SSPPs TL and microstrip line, complex structure and large conversion size are required for mode conversion. To solve this problem, we design a compact transition structure from microstrip line to SSPPs TL. The defect ground structure in the upper layer and the artificial magnetic conductor in the lower layer together constitute the ISGW structure, which helps to improve the antenna gain. Finally achieves a scanning angle of 71° in the bandwidth range of 25GHz-35GHz, and the gain is stable at 10dBi, and the radiation efficiency is above 95%.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Circularly Polarized Rectenna for Wireless Power Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a single-fed circularly polarized (CP) rectenna is proposed at 2.45 GHz for applications of wireless power harvesting (WPH). The antenna is a square patch antenna which generates circularly polarized CP radiation by cutting the diagonal. The antenna is designed to be integrated with a rectifier circuit through a quarter-wavelength impedance converter and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{50}\ \mathbf{\Omega}$</tex> feed line. The simulation results indicate that the antenna has excellent radiation effect at 2.45 GHz. The RF-DC conversion efficiency can reach over 30% within the input power range of -12.12 dBm to 7.68 dBm, and a maximum RF-DC conversion efficiency of 65.35% can be obtained when the input power is 2.92 dBm.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Gain Endfire Filtering Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband high-gain endfire antenna with filtering function is proposed. By combining the filter and vivaldi antenna and manipulating the mutual coupling between them, The filtering function is realized. Gradual choke slots are used to reduce antenna side lobes and improve front and back ratio, A spoof surface plasmon waveguide is introduced at the open end to improve its gain and obtain good end-fire performance, the average gain has increased by 4dB. The designed antenna has a relative bandwidth of 55.6%, an average gain of 11.6dBi in the bandwidth, and an out-of-band rejection of more than 15dB.

articleTitle: A UWB-MIMO Antenna Based on Decoupling of EBG and Ground Branches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a UWB-MIMO antenna based on decoupling of EBG and ground branches is designed. The design uses a conical feed line to feed a slotted elliptical monopole antenna, achieving an impedance bandwidth of 3.8GHz to 12.4GHz (relative bandwidth of 106%). At the same time, a defect ground structure and T-shaped, H-shaped ground branches are used for decoupling, resulting in an isolation degree of less than -20dB between the four feeding ports within the antenna operating frequency band. In addition, The antenna also has stable radiation direction and excellent gain performance.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Metal-Insulator-Metal Metasurface Based on Equivalent Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Metasurfaces formed of two-dimensional array of tailored meta-atoms has the capability to control the transmission and reflection electromagnetic waves in subwavelength scale. The flexibility in designing meta-atom makes the design process involve iterative full wave simulation, which is time-consuming and labor-intensive. To accelerate the design process, this paper proposes a method based on an equivalent circuit model and deep learning network to predict the forward response and perform inverse design of metal-insulator-metal (MIM) metasurfaces. We introduce an equivalent circuit modeling approach to analysis the response of MIM metasurfaces. The equivalent circuit model combines with deep learning networks to predict the optical response of metasurfaces and perform inverse design of the structural geometric parameters for desired responses. By comparing the prediction results with full-wave simulation results, we demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Non-Uniform Distributed Parameter Field Line Coupling Model for High-Power Microwave
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, based on the classical low frequency field line coupling model and the high frequency transmission line distribution parameter model in the transmission line super theory, a high frequency field line coupling model with non-uniform distribution parameters for high-power microwave (HPM) is proposed. In this model, the distribution parameters of the line varying with the position can be used to describe the coupling characteristics of the transmission line, and the load response current generated by HPM can be quickly calculated on a line by combining with the finite difference time domain method. Compared with the classical low frequency field line coupling model, the proposed model in this paper is more consistent with the load response current waveform calculated by CST.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis of ship RCS: based on sea surface design and different radar wave incidence angles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The letter evaluates the performance of a ship target's radar cross section (RCS) using a commonly used over-the-horizon radar's plane wave at 28 MHz. In contrast to prior work, we conduct a comprehensive analysis by simultaneously considering the following factors: (i) 3D modeling of a ship target, (ii) varying plane wave incidence angles, and (iii) the influence of sea surface clutter. Our simulation study shows that the RCS of the same ship target can vary significantly at different incident angles of the plane waves, primarily due to the complex ship structure.

articleTitle: FDTD Solution for Signal Transmission in Plasma Sheath
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An inhomogeneous ionized plasma layer is generated around the hypersonic vehicle, which may cause radio blackout. In this paper, an innovative multi-physical method combining plasma fluid equations and Maxwell's equations is proposed. Numerical results indicate that the electron concentration can be significantly reduced via the applied magnetic field to create a magnetic window. In addition, this paper proposes a set of simulation methods to realize the process of receiving signals from hypersonic vehicle, avoiding complicated and expensive flight experiments. Providing theoretical basis and simulation data for solving the problem of radio blackout in engineering. This is also one of the innovations of this article, therefore, our research has an extensive application prospect.

articleTitle: Inversion of Equivalent Ground Conductivity Based on Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The measured inversion method is the fundamental method to obtain the equivalent ground conductivity. This method uses the measured results of the electric wave propagation field strength and delay, combined with the theoretical prediction method of electric wave propagation, to invert the ground conductivity along the propagation path. In this article, the integral equation method was selected as the forward algorithm, and the mean square error between the theoretical prediction results of the propagation delay correction and the measured results was used as the optimization goal. The artificial fish swarm algorithm was chosen as the inversion algorithm, and the Kriging interpolation was used to optimize the inversion rate. Finally, the feasibility of this inversion method and the reliability of the inverted conductivity were verified through simulation experiments in some test areas.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Transmitarray Phaser Using Vivaldi Antenna for Dispersive Delay Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband transmitarray antenna for dispersive delay radiation based Vivaldi antenna operating at 0.1 THz band is presented. The unit cell consists of two Vivaldi antennas that transmit and receive signals and a linear group delay engineering non-common-pass transmission line network. The whole structure is designed on the low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) substrate and can achieve 0.06ns variation of phase group delay in the operating band (75-105GHz) which can operates as a phaser. The return loss of the whole system is greater than 17 dB in the operating band, indicating that the structure can be practically processed. The proposed transmi-tar ray antenna phasers have potential applications in reducing the accuracy requirements of digital-to-analog converters and in millimeter-wave and terahertz analog signal processing.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis of monostatic Scattering Problems for Three-dimensional Objects Using Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a combination of characteristic basis functions (CBFs) method and compressive sensing (CS) is utilized to accelerate the solution of monostatic scattering problems. Different from the dense matrix equation of the traditional method of moments (MOM), the proposed method transforms the dense matrix equation of the traditional MOM into an underdetermined equation, and then substitutes the CBFs as sparse transformation matrix into the underdetermined equation. Finally, the least square method is selected as the recovery algorithm to restore the induced current. The numerical simulation results are given to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: A Reflective Ultra-Broadband Polarized Rotating Surface with Simple Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a reflective ultra-broadband linearly polarized rotating artificial electromagnetic material is proposed. Its unit is composed of a double-opening resonant ring and a metal ground sheet separated by a dielectric substrate. Simulation results show that the polarized rotating surface(PRS) can resonate at three frequencies under incident electromagnetic waves, which leads to an increase in the bandwidth of cross-polarized reflections. The designed polarization rotation surface can convert the line polarization electromagnetic wave to its cross-polarization electromagnetic wave in the frequency range of 6.25 GHz~18.95 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 100% and the polarization rotation efficiency is greater than 90% throughout the bandwidth. The proposed polarization rotation surface has an extremely simple geometry and a wider bandwidth compared to the currently published related designs. Therefore, this reflective polarization rotation surface has potential applications in areas such as polarization control.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband Metasurface Antenna Based on Hybrid Via-Wall Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, a compact broadband metasurface (MTS) antenna using hybrid via-wall structures is firstly proposed. First, different via-wall MTS structures are derived from a conventional square MTS structure by folding the square patches downward and loading stacked patches horizontally in various configurations. These modifications effectively lower the resonance frequency and enable miniaturization to varying degrees. Furtherly, for a multi-resonance wideband feature, a hybrid MTS structure consisting of different via-wall structures is presented and then utilized to construct a MTS-based antenna by employing a slot-coupled feeding structure. With these hybrid via-wall structures that resonant at different frequencies, the MTS-based antenna can exhibit a wideband impedance matching. Finally, Theoretical results demonstrate that the proposed antenna achieves remarkable performance. It features a wide impedance bandwidth of 53.4% (5.41~9.35GHz) and delivers a high gain of approximately 5.9dBi within a compact overall size only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.44\lambda_{0}\times 0.44\lambda_{0}\times 0.07 \lambda_{0}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Thermal-Stress Multiphysics Simulation of Microwave Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multiphysics simulation method for microwave amplifiers, integrating electromagnetic, thermal, and stress analyses. By combining the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD), finite-element time-domain (FETD), and finite element method (FEM), highly accurate simulations are performed. At last, the method is applied to analyze the multiphysics effects of a microwave amplifier, providing comprehensive insights into its performance characteristics.

articleTitle: Accurate Solution of Volume Integral Equations for Electromagnetic Problems with Highly Inhomogeneous Media
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Electromagnetic problems can be formulated by an integral equation method and volume integral equations (VIEs) are indispensable to govern the problems with inhomogeneous media. Although the surface integral equations (SIEs) are preferred for the problems with some layered-inhomogeneous media, they are unable to accommodate arbitrarily-inhomogeneous media which the VIEs can describe. Also, VIEs belong to the second-kind of integral equations which can result in well-conditioned system matrices. However, the traditional method of moments (MoM) with the Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson (SWG) basis function may not be able to give accurate solutions since it has to assume homogeneous media in each tetrahedral elements. In this paper, the Nyström method is used to solve the VIEs with highly-inhomogeneous media. Since the method uses current densities as unknown functions to be solved, the integral kernels do not include material parameters and they are only related to the free-space Green's function, leading to well-conditioned system matrices no matter how different the materials are in the VIEs. A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the method and its good performance is verified.

articleTitle: A Method for Predicting Time-Domain Radiation Characteristics for Bowtie Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A method for predicting the time-domain radiation characteristics of bowtie antenna is proposed in this paper. The simplification of the bowtie antenna is accomplished and modeled by a combination of two V-shaped dipoles. Then, the radiated waveforms and peak field intensity patterns of bowtie antenna are obtained through the current distribution of V-shaped dipole. Numerical validation demonstrates the effectiveness of the presented method in time-domain performance prediction for bowtie antenna. Furthermore, a brief discussion on the application of the method in antenna design and time-domain pattern synthesis of array antenna is made.

articleTitle: A Near Field Electromagnetic Calculation Method for Complex Target Involving Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A near field electromagnetic calculation method for dielectric media is introduced in this paper. The method is based on the algorithm of shooting and bouncing rays (SBR). In this method, a point source is introduced to display the antenna. The tracing rays emitted from the point source are used to approximate the near field electromagnetic wave. The near field effect to the incident electromagnetic field and the transmission/reflection of the dielectric media are induced to propagation calculation. The proposed algorithm is able to calculate the near field electromagnetics of dielectric media.

articleTitle: On the Efficient Scattering Analysis from Targets with Surface Discontinuities Using An Extended Half-RWG Basis Function
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The surface discontinuities in the form of cylindrical protrusions or dents such as rivets, are ubiquities on modern aircraft surfaces and cause significant scattering in certain incident angles. Due to the large contrast in spatial scale between the surface discontinuity and the aircraft body, the full-wave scattering analysis for them is technically challenging in both mesh generation and numerical simulation. This paper proposes an extended Half-RWG (EH-RWG) basis function for the cylindrical-shaped surface discontinuities. The EH-RWG basis function adds a rectangular area based on the conventional Half-RWG basis function; hence the current distribution on the cylinder side surface can be modeled without additional mesh elements. Based on the integral equation discontinuous Galerkin (IEDG) method, the proposed method allows a flexible mesh generation. It improves the simulation efficiency for targets with this particular kind of surface discontinuity. Numerical experiments on low-RCS testbeds verify the accuracy and robustness of the EH-RWG basis function.

articleTitle: A Low Sidelobe Ka Band Circle-Aperture Conical Scanning Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a low sidelobe Ka band circle-aperture conical scanning phased array antenna is proposed. This antenna array consists of 148 E-shaped patch antenna elements in circular configuration. Simulation results show the phased array antenna can achieve conical scanning of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 25^{\circ}$</tex>. The active voltage standing wave ratios (AVSWRs) are less than 2 in the range of 30.5-39.5GHz, with a relative bandwidth of about 25.7% and the sidelobe level is lower than -22dB. This proposed antenna using PCB technology has a wide range of applications in the field of millimeter wave communication, especially for radar seeker.

articleTitle: High-Dimensional Uncertainty Quantification for Radar Cross Section of Multi-Layered Dieletric Block
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: We propose an uncertainty quantification method for Radar Cross Section (RCS) of multi-layered dieletric block. Due to the numerous components and complex shape of the dielectric block, traditional intrusive uncertainty quantification methods, requiring significant modifications to the origin solver, are no longer feasible. In addition, the important material parameters of each multi-layered dielectric block component are considered in uncertainty quantification, leading to high-dimensional uncertainty. As a result, the uncertainty quantification of RCS becomes even more challenging. To address these issues, based on a data-driven ideology, we construct a surrogate model from a sparse dataset to enable fast prediction of the RCS, and thereby extract the statistical characteristics of the RCS to achieve rapid and efficient uncertainty quantification.

articleTitle: A Broadband Millimeter Wave Fixed-Beam Leaky-Wave Antenna with Stable Broadside Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In point-to-point wireless communication, antennas need to radiate in a fixed direction with broadband property. However, the traditional leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is limited in broadband applications because of the beam squint effect. In this paper, a broadband fixed-beam LWA radiating at broadside is designed. A parallel plate filled with dielectric substrate is loaded on the leakage side of a ridge gap waveguide (RGW), by designing the shape of the loaded dielectric slab, the beam can be fixed at broadside in a wide frequency band of 58% (from 22 to 40 GHz). The radiation angle changes only 2.3°at broadside in the band, and the gain only has a slight deviation of 0.8 dB, which shows a good stability.

articleTitle: Performance Enhanced Millimeter-Wave Array Antenna by Sequentially Rotating Wideband Circularly Polarized Radiating Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A performance enhanced circularly polarized (CP) 2×2 array antenna is constructed by sequentially rotating four wideband CP radiating elements. It is a multilayered structure based on standard printed circuit board (PCB) processing. A microstrip feeding network is designed to provide the required excitation phases and amplitudes for the four radiating elements in a wide operating band. According to the simulated results, the proposed low-profile wide-band antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\sim 47.96$</tex> GHz, an axial ratio bandwidth within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\sim 46.16$</tex> GHz and an average in-band gain higher than 5dBic, etc, thus, making it an attractive candidate for the future wireless communications.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Canopy Layer of Forest Trees on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Signal Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The influence of tree canopy layers on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) signal transmission in forest environments is studied. The stable transmission of signals is very important for the design of reliable wireless communication systems for UAVs. Therefore, a forest model is established to analyze the attenuation of the signal based on the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method. And the attenuation of the signal is analyzed in canopy layers of different thicknesses. The numerical results show that after passing through the canopy, the average attenuation of the signal is 35.32 dB.

articleTitle: Research on solving time-dependent Schrodinger equation for higher-order FDTD based on spatial filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Combining the spatial filtering (SF) technique with FDTD(2, q) method (2 and q denote the temporal differential order and spatial differential order, respectively), a novel SF-FDTD(2, q) method with more relaxed Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) condition is proposed and used for solving 3D time-dependent Schrödinger equation. Then, the correctness of the SF-FDTD(2, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>) method is validated by calculating eigenfrequencies of the 3D quantum well model.

articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose Effects of A 180 nm Bulk CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: CMOS devices are widely used in modern integrated circuits. However, like any semiconductor device, CMOS devices are susceptible to total ionizing dose (TID) effects when exposed to ionizing radiation environments. In this work, a TCAD model of a 180 nm bulk COMS is developed to investigate the impact of TID effects. Simulated results show that the TID effects can cause a negative shift in the voltage characteristics curve and an increase in leakage current of CMOS devices.

articleTitle: A Phaseless SRM for Radiated Emission Modeling of PCBs in Shielding Enclosures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an improved source reconstruction method for modeling radiated emissions of printed circuit boards (PCBs) in shielding enclosures using single-plane phaseless near-field scanning. Numerical Green's function is used to establish a relationship between the input near-field data and equivalent source to ensure the accuracy of source reconstruction. To retrieve phase information from the magnitude-only near-field data, an iteration approach is developed by dividing the NF data into two parts with an assumed initial phase. Two numerical examples are presented to validate efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multiband Radar Signal Fusion Based on Double Threshold Sparsity Adaptive Matching Pursuit
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel multiband fusion method named double threshold sparsity adaptive matching pursuit (DTSAMP) to improve the range resolution of radar. In particularly, the adaptive threshold and step size is designed to improve the precision of parameter estimation and resist the effects of noise. Based on sparse reconstruction (SR) theory and the geometry theory of diffraction (GTD) model, sparse subbands complete incoherent compensation, and then coherent subbands are utilized to obtain a full-band signal by DTSAMP. Also, the proposed method does not require prior information on the number of scattering centers. Simulations verify the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-band Dual-polarized Two-layer Microstrip Patch Antenna with Dual-port Feeding
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band dual-polarized microstrip patch antenna is proposed. The antenna is composed of two-layer printed-circuit boards. Two mutually perpendicular microstrip lines are used for feeding on the top of the lower-bottom printed-circuit board, and four symmetrical equal square patches are placed on the top of the upper printed-circuit board. The proposed antenna has two frequency bands. The first center frequency is 4.32 GHz and the second center frequency is 5.86 GHz. The port isolation of the antenna is larger than 15dB in both working bands. The suggested antenna has linear polarization as its polarization characteristic. It shows perfect radiation performance in two frequency bands, where the difference between co-polarization and cross-polarization in the principal radiation direction is larger than 20dB.

articleTitle: A Low Profile and Broadband Pattern Reconfigurable Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile and broadband pattern reconfigurable dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed. Four different radiation patterns, including one conical pattern, two tilted patterns and one broadside pattern, are realized by changing the phase difference of the two excitation ports. The antenna has a broad impedance bandwidth of 15.1% (3.37-3.9 GHz) with a low profile of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.1\lambda 0$</tex>. The simulated antenna gains of 5.42 dBi, 8 dBi and 8.48 dBi are achieved over the impedance bandwidth for conical, tilted, and broadside patterns, respectively. The antenna is a good candidate for 5G complex communication applications.

articleTitle: A Brief Review of HEMP Scaled Model Test
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The scaled model test is an alternative method for high altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) illumination test. Theoretical basis of the scaled model test is introduced briefly first. Then scaled model test activities in HEMP field are retrospect. Several considerations when doing a scaled model test plan are analyzed at last.

articleTitle: A Polarization Conversion Metasurface with Bidirectional Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a linear to circular polarization metasurface converter with bidirectional scattering is presented. When a linearly polarized wave impinges on the metasurface, it is converted into a left-handed circularly polarized wave with half reflection and half transmission. A sandwich structure unit cell operating at 3.65 GHz is design to realize the bidirectional scattering function, which consists of a pair of square patches with two circular holes on the top and bottom layers, a middle ground layer and two metal vias connecting the top and bottom layers. The proposed metasurface is demonstrated by principle analysis and full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Study on Design of Steeply Dropped Wide Passband Frequency Selective Surface Operating in X-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A steeply-descent wide-passband frequency selective surface (FSS) operating in the X-band is introduced. It has a cell size of 0.2 λand a center operating frequency of 10.0 GHz. It is able to achieve a transmission efficiency of more than 80% in the frequency range of 6.30 GHz-10.70 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of 94%. The right side of its passband forms a good steep drop characteristic with a relative bandwidth of 4.4%, and there is a drop stopband with| S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>|≤-40 dB at 15.67 GHz. The structure shows good operation characteristics and polarization stability, when the incident angle is 0-50°. For further verification, FSS is processed and tested in kind.

articleTitle: Direct Solution of MoM Matrix Equation Using Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury Formula-Based Algorithm with Lagrange Interpolations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this article, the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury (SMW) formula is applied to accelerate the direct solution of electromagnetic scattering problem for three-dimensional (3D) perfect electric conducting (PEC) objects with the Lagrange interpolations. To speed up the direct solution of the matrix equation, the dense impedance matrix is transformed into products of several diagonal matrix blocks via the SMW formula. The Lagrange interpolation algorithm effectively compresses the matrices of far blocks interactions. The numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Nonuniform Transmission Line Model for Electromagnetic Radiation in Uniform Lossy Medium
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The electromagnetic systems in submarine objects may generate electromagnetic radiation in seawater and pose a risk of exposing the submarines to hostile detector.
