It is of significance to investigate the radiation property of objects submerged in seawater. In this paper, the seawater is considered as a uniform lossy medium, and the electromagnetic radiation in it is analyzed with spherical expansion method. Especially, the nonuniform transmission line model (NTL) for electromagnetic radiation in free space is extended to uniform lossy media. Some numerical results of the equivalent parameters of the NTL models are examined.

articleTitle: Design of 1–6 GHz GaAs-based Monolithic Limiter and Measurements of its Power Handling Capability under HPM Pulses
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this article, a 1–6 GHz monolithic integrated limiter with a size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.4\ \text{mm} \times 1.8\ \text{mm}$</tex> was designed and fabricated in gallium arsenide (GaAs) PIN technology. The binary power splitting typology is employed in the first stage of the proposed limiter to enhance the power handling capability. The measurement results show that the insertion loss is less than 0.6 dB. The return loss is better than 12 dB within the operating band. the maximum power handling capability of the limiter is up to 61 dBm at a 3 us input pulse with a repetition frequency of 50 Hz. The leakage power level is lower than 17 dBm.

articleTitle: Research on the Scattering Characteristics of Double Exponential Time-Varying Profile Moving Plasma
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The plasma sheath generated around a high-speed moving object is usually time-varying. The time-varying characteristics will have an impact on the electromagnetic (EM) scattering properties of the target, which is not conducive to the monitoring and identification of the target by ground radar stations. In this study, the backscattering and the radar cross section (RCS) of a double-exponential time-varying profile moving plasma target are studied by combining the shift-operator finite-difference time-domain (SO-FDTD) method and Lorentz transformation.

articleTitle: Reverse Design of a Dual-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna Based on Binary Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> compact dual-band microstrip patch antenna operating at 2.18 and 2.45 GHz is proposed in this paper. The patch area of the antenna is discretized into small squares of the same size, and the binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) algorithm is used to search for the optimal arrangement of these squares. Compared with traditional patch antenna design method, the proposed intelligent algorithm-assisted design method saves optimization time and provides distinct antenna performance.

articleTitle: Large-Area Pseudospin and Valley Waveguide States in a Three-Layer Heterostructure System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Topological pseudospin- and valley-dependent edge states have been widely explored due to their inherent topological properties and easy implementations. Conventional methods create topological modes tightly confined at the interfaces, which hinders high-capacity energy transport and efficient interconnection with diverse devices. Here, we propose a tri-band three-layer heterostructure system supporting both large-area pseudospin- and valley-locked waveguide states. Both unidirectional excitation and backscattering-immune propagation have been demonstrated. Besides, the large-area waveguide states manifest tunable mode width, which can be potentially used for impedance matching with wave-guiding channels with different aperture widths. This work enlarges the photonic systems that could be utilized for multi-band multi-functionallarge-area-mode enabled topological devices.

articleTitle: Markov Channel Modeling for Time-Varying Loran Singal with Joint Amplitude and Phase
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Channel modeling helps developers understand the wireless channel environment and can reduce expenses when developing new technologies. We propose a joint amplitude and phase modeling method for loran signals. We establish a realtime monitoring system to obtain real signal delay and fading data. The statistical properties of the a priori data are reproduced by dividing the data states and using the Markov chain method. The results with the first-order statistical properties show that the algorithm has a good probability density distribution fit and integral probability density distribution.

articleTitle: A Novel Learning Scheme for Inversely-Designing Bonding Wire With Multi-fidelity Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for efficiently designing bonding wire (BW) using multi-fidelity data assistance. The proposed learning framework consists of two key components: an inversion network and a residual network. The inversion network is utilized to understand the complex relationship between the performance of the BW and its structural parameters within the low-fidelity model space. On the other hand, the residual network is employed to capture the differences between the low-fidelity and high-fidelity data. By combining these networks in a cascaded manner, we can effectively carry out inverse design for the BW. The method achieves an average testing accuracy of 95.62% based on 3000 tests. Notably, compared to traditional forward optimization approaches, our proposed method can fulfill the design requirements in just a fraction of seconds. To validate our approach experimentally, we weld the BW designed using our method onto the microstrip line and perform a de-embedding process. The measured performance aligns well with the design specifications, confirming the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: A Compact and Wideband Dielectric Resonator Magnetoelectric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with magnetoelectric dipole (ME-dipole) characteristic is proposed. The linearly single-polarized antenna prototype is composed of a foam-supported elevated dielectric block fed by a differential metal semi-loop probe. The DRA element in its <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{\delta 11}^{x}$</tex> mode and its metal feeding probe are equivalent to an orthogonal magnetic dipole (MD) and electric dipole (ED), respectively. With an appropriate combination of these two dipole modes, the proposed design achieves a broadside unidirectional radiation with low backward radiation and equal E-plane and H-plane radiation patterns. To verify the design concept, a dual-polarized antenna with the electrical size of 0.42λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.42λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.12λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is designed and analyzed. The simulated front-to-back (FBR) ratio of the proposed antenna is better than 22 dB with 20% relative bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Novel Measurement Method of Complex Permittivity Based on a 8.5-GHz $\text{TM}_{010}$ Cavity Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel measurement method for the complex per-mittivity of materials is proposed based on a cavity resonator with the use of perturbation method. The cavity resonator is simulated and designed by the well-known HFSS software, and then physically fabricated. Three kinds of low-loss materials are sampled and measured at 8.5 GHz by the physical device. The experimental results show that the relative errors of measured dielectric constant and loss tangent for Teflon materials are within 0.1 % and 11 %, respectively, and they are more accurate compared with the results of other measurement methods. The measured results validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Wideband Matched Filtering Antennas with Absorptive Resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a design method of filtering antennas with wide matching bands to realize the integration of multiple functions such as absorbing, filtering, and radiating, and protect the system as well. In our design, an absorptive stub is employed to absorb the out-of-band signals. As such, a cascaded topology with lossy stubs, lossless stubs, and the resonant antenna is proposed to acquire the absorptive filtering antenna. The characteristic of the absorptive stub, and the response of the equivalent circuit are specifically analyzed here. Finally, an absorptive filtering slot antenna is implemented to prove that the method can be used to achieve a matching bandwidth far beyond that of a conventional resonant antenna.

articleTitle: A Wideband Polarization-Insensitive Switchable Absorber/Reflector Based on Active Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this article, a switchable polarization-insensitive ultra-wideband absorber/reflector reconfigurable metasurface is proposed. The proposed structure consists of the top active metasurface layer, three patterned resistive films, and a simple bias network layer. The metasurface contains a square ring and four pairs of PIN diodes, The PIN diodes are controlled by the bias networks through the metalized via holes to obtain the switchable properties. The metasurface can achieve an absorptivity of around 85% over a frequency band ranging from 0.57 to 17.2 GHz under the absorption state. Under the reflection state, a reflectivity of greater than 50% is achieved over a frequency band ranging from 3 to 11.7 GHz. Due to the symmetrical structure of the metasurface, the metasurface remains polarization-insensitive. In addition, the metasurface has a profile of about 0.08 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _{0}\ (\lambda_{0}$</tex> represents the wavelength at the lowest frequency point).

articleTitle: A Study of 100ns double beam bunch distribute system for SXFEL
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To improve the utilization efficiency of the linear accelerator, Shanghai Soft X-ray Free-Electron Laser (SXFEL), plans to upgrade to double bunch mode with a bunch time separation of 100 ns and a maximum repetition rate of 50 Hz. A new beam distribute system is designed to separate the 100 ns beam bunch by bunch. The beam distribute system consists of four kicker magnets and one septum magnets. This paper presents the design of beam bunch distribute system.

articleTitle: Mixed- Precision Algorithm in Electromagnetic Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Single-precision algorithms are known to offer superior computational efficiency compared to double-precision algorithms. However, achieving the same level of computational accuracy as double-precision algorithms in single-precision arithmetic can be challenging. Mixed-precision algorithms have emerged as a promising solution to this problem. In this study, we employ a mixed-precision algorithm to solve the matrix equation Ax=b generated by the electromagnetic finite element method. Specifically, single-precision arithmetic is utilized in the matrix factorization phase, whereas double-precision arithmetic is applied in the residual calculation and iterative refinement phase. Our experimental results demonstrate that the mixed-precision algorithm achieves computational efficiency that is approximately 1.5 times higher than that of the double-precision algorithm, and occupies 40% less memory. Additionally, the computational accuracy of the mixed-precision algorithm is found to meet the requirements of double-precision arithmetic.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband 3dB Quadrature Coupler Based on Offset-Coupled Striplines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a 3dB quadrature coupler based on multisection coupler and offset-coupled striplines is presented. Wide bandwidth with better amplitude balance is obtained by connecting two 8.34dB multisection uniform coupled-line coupler in series with compensated matching stubs. The proposed coupler consists of a three-layer printed circuit board. The proposed design has the bandwidth larger than 125% from 2GHz to 12GHz. Measurements show that the given design can achieve coupling coefficient of 3.7±0.8dB and phase difference between the two output ports of 86°±4° in the whole operation band.

articleTitle: High-Performance Simulation of Electromagnetic Scattering by 3D Objects Using the GPU-accelerated Parallel MLFMA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-performance massively parallel multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) on clusters with graphics processing units (GPUs) accelerators. ELLPACK format-based schemes are proposed to ensure a high computational throughput for GPU accelerated evaluation of interpolation and anterpolation operations in MLFMA. The program is further optimized using the mechanism of stream and the shared-memory/register hierarchical memory architecture of GPU. The implementation of all the proposed techniques make the aggregation/disaggregation calculations an order of magnitude faster than the conventional ones, and halved the iteration time for an aircraft model with 10 billion unknowns, which is a significant progress in GPU accelerated massively parallel MLFMA.

articleTitle: Fusion of LiDAR and MMW Radar Point Clouds for Environment Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: 3D environment sensing and modeling plays a crucial role in many domains. To acquire more detailed and comprehensive environmental information, this paper proposes a fusion system of LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) and millimeter-wave (mmw) SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar). The system utilizes a custom-built hardware platform to collect data from both LiDAR and SAR sensors. The point cloud data acquired from the two sensors is precisely fused using the ICP (Iterative Closest Point) algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate the significant robustness of the fusion system and successful achievement of high-precision fusion of LiDAR and SARdata.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Wideband Antenna with Dual Notch Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A planar printed dual-notch ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna with a cup-shaped radiating patch and trapezoidal ground plane is proposed in this paper. By optimizing the microstrip line and using the defected ground structure (DGS) technique on the ground plane, the antenna achieves a bandwidth coverage of 2.5GHz-14GHz. Two notch slots were respectively etched on the radiating patch and ground plane, resulting in two notched bands to effectively prevent signal interference from the WiMAX (3.3-3.8 GHz) and WLAN (5.15-5.825 GHz) frequency bands. Additionally, the proposed antenna exhibits good omni-directional performance within the working band, making it suitable for various UWB communication systems.

articleTitle: A hybrid interpolation method for the high-efficient frequency sweep in electromagnetic simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the integration of the rational vectorfitting into the model-based parameter estimation (MBPE) technique is proposed to accelerate numerical simulations of electromagnetic simulation. The poles and zeros in the frequency band will be extracted by rational vector-fitting method, and the band is divided into several monotonous intervals. The MBPE is then applied to easily interpolate the frequency points in each monotonous interval. The example result of antenna array shows that the improved adaptive frequency sweep method reduces the number of frequency points required for direct calculation. The accuracy and effectiveness of this method are verified.

articleTitle: Field Focusing in Bianisotropic Zero-index Media through Growing Evanescent Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, we show the field focusing in a realizable medium exhibiting electromagnetic properties of zero permittivity and permeability together with bianisotropy. Electric and magnetic field solutions in the medium are decoupled and have an exponential factor with opposite signs of exponents, featuring exponentially growing/decaying evanescent waves. By engineering the direction of bianisotropy, we show both the ID and 2D electric field focusing, along with the decaying magnetic field. Our work provides a new mechanism for field focusing and could find applications in energy harvesting, nonlinearity enhancement, etc.

articleTitle: Linear Array Thinning Using JAYA-Iterative Fourier Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid algorithm, namely JAYA-iterative Fourier technique (JAYA-IFT), is presented for linear array thinning. This algorithm is based on the combination of two methods, JAYA and the iterative Fourier technique (IFT). JAYA serves as the primary framework of the algorithm while IFT is utilized to refine the best solution in each iteration. By this means, the IFT is incorporated into the algorithm as prior knowledge to facilitate and improve convergence. Two linear array syntheses were carried out using the proposed JAYA-IFT method. Numerical results were provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Compact and Broadband Microstrip Patch Antenna Based on the Flexible Magnetic Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A flexible microstrip patch antenna using a dielectric-magnetic composite substrate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ni}_{.5}\text{Zn}_{0.5}\text{Fe}2\mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> (NZO)/rubber is proposed. The ferrite NZO reduces the antenna size and increases the bandwidth, while the rubber lowers the losses and enhances the flexibility. The substrate has suitable dielectric and magnetic properties in the S and C bands (2-8GHz), with a dielectric constant of 3.5-4.0, a permeability of 1.1-1.7, and a loss tangent of about 0.1. We fabricated a circular microstrip patch antenna (diameter 50 mm, thickness 5 mm, patch size 31.5mm) with an operating frequency of 2.227GHz and a bandwidth of 290 MHz (12.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), which matches well with the simulation results. This work shows that dielectric-magnetic substrates can enable miniaturization and broadband in antenna design.

articleTitle: Three Simulation Methods of Coaxial Feeding in FDTD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Three coaxial feeding methods in FDTD simulation is studied in this paper. More accurate S-parameters are obtained by using the simulation of coaxial feed. This study also shows that both simulation of coaxial feeding and probe feeding work equally well. The simulation results of S-parameters and running times obtained by three methods are also compared.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Ultra-Wideband Energy-Selective Surface for High-Power Microwave Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A flexible energy-selective surface (ESS) with ultrawide band protection is proposed for adaptive high-power microwave protection in the field of electromagnetic biological effects in this paper. By loading the nonlinear device such as PIN diode on the frequency selection surface, the goal of electromagnetic protection will be achieved. Simulation results show that the ESS achieves an insertion loss of less than 3 dB over the frequency range of 3.5-4.5 GHz at a low power level. Additionally, the ESS provides ultra-wide protection against HPM in the frequency range of 0.1-6.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Frequency-Selective Rasorber with Switchable Second-Order Bandpass Response
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel technique is presented for achieving a dual-polarized A-T-A rasorber with a switchable second-order bandpass response. The lossy layer is formed by embedding resonators in a centrally symmetrical manner into the square ring unit. The lossless layer is constructed using a patch-grid coupling structure, thereby enabling the rasorber to exhibit a second-order bandpass response. P-i-n diodes are integrated into the structure, and the symmetric bias design allows for effective control of the passband in dual-polarized scenarios. By toggling the state of the p-i-n diodes, the transparent window in 2.88-3.16 GHz can be triggered, exhibiting sharp roll-off edges. When the window is closed, wideband absorption is achieved in 1.3-4.0 GHz. Details of the proposed reconfigurable rasorber are discussed.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Dual-Polarization Folded Crossed Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this letter, a low-profile dual-polarization folded crossed dipole antenna based on multiplayer plate technology is proposed to realize the miniaturization of the antenna. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> phased array antenna has been improved based on this unit using the method of phase extinction of induced currents. The results show that the overall height of the antenna is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.005}\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex>, and the 3dB bandwidth of the cell is 118°. The sub-array designed on this basis can achieve a scan angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{50}^{\circ}$</tex> in both y-polarization and x-polarization.

articleTitle: Simulation and Design of A Two-Axis Electrostatically Driven MOEMS Micromirror Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Recently, MEMS micromirrors have been widely used for in-vehicle LiDAR with the development of automated driving. This paper presents a two-axis electrostatically driven micromirror. Firstly, the torsional modes and resonant frequencies of the two-axis electrostatically driven micromirror along the X-axis and Y-axis are obtained by theoretical formula. And the 3D modeling of the micromirror is performed. Then, the resonant frequency of the MEMS micromirror is simulated using the finite element method. The simulation results of two deflection motion modes of MEMS mirror are basically consistent with the theoretical calculation results. The maximum mechanical deflection angles of the micromirror along the X-axis and Y-axis under 50V drive are 12° and 7.96° at a resonance frequency of 3605.3Hz and 14451Hz, respectively.

articleTitle: A C-Band Microwave and Optical Integrated Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The design, fabrication and measurement of an integrated antenna array which combines C-band microwave antennas and optical antennas are introduced. The proposed antenna array consists of strip-line Vivaldi antennas, a common metal frame which acts as ground plate for Vivaldi antennas, and an optical antenna. The prototype array exhibits a measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 2.5$</tex> and good radiation pattern from 5.0GHz to 6.0GHz, showing well agreement with simulations. In addition, a good imaging capability of the integrated antenna array is presented in the imaging test.

articleTitle: Design of Energy Selective Surface with Ultra-Wideband Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband energy selective surface (ESS) is proposed and simulated to protect electronic devices from high power microwaves (HPM). The ESS consists of two bandpass metasurfaces cascaded with an active metasurface. The performance of this structure has been studied using equivalent circuit models and full-wave simulations. The results show that the operating center frequency at 5 GHz with insertion loss of 0.4 dB, the insertion loss (IL) is less than 1 dB in the range from 4.77 GHz to 5.78 GHz, during the range from 1 GHz to 9 GHz, the shielding efficiency (SE) of HPM exceed 20 dB, and the relative bandwidth reaches 160%. At the same time, the structure has a certain degree of polarization insensitivity and superior angular stability.

articleTitle: Simulation of a New Corrugated Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a new corrugated horn antenna ranges from 40 GHz to 60GHz is simulated based on the static zone performance of the compact field, which satisfies measurement demands of feed antenna. After simulation and optimization, main parameters of the antenna, such as standing-wave coefficient, radiation pattern and radiation gain are highly improved, comparing with the traditional antenna.

articleTitle: Broadband High Gain Low-Profile Antenna Based on Metasurface of Cell Size Gradient
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a double-layer metasurface antenna with wide band, high gain and low profile based on rhomboid element size gradient structure is proposed. Based on the mechanism that the non-uniformly distributed patch element structure can expand the bandwidth, a metasurface with rhombic element size gradient structure is proposed to expand the bandwidth. The non-uniformly distributed array can also improve the radiation efficiency of the antenna. The thickness of the metasurface antenna is only 0.07 times the maximum wavelength of the operating frequency, the −10dB impedance bandwidth reaches 49%(4.49~7.42GHz), the 3dB gain bandwidth reaches 43%(4. 17~6.45GHz), and the peak gain is as high as 10.78dBi, which completely has the excellent characteristics of wide band, high gain and low profile.

articleTitle: Tumour-Treating Fields: Electric Field Simulation of Human Brain with Alternating Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Tumor-Treating Fields (TTFields) is a novel antimitotic cancer treatment modality which disrupts cancer cell replication. The applied electric field is in a low frequency range, which can be approximated as quasi-static field. The Poisson equation is applied in the literature for simulating the field distribution in human brain. However, most works ignore the effects of applied voltage frequency and the relative permittivity of human brain tissue. In this paper, a quasi-static model is developed and the modes of the complex Poisson equation are obtained by considering the effects of voltage frequency and permittivity of human brain tissue. The mixed Dirichlet-Neumann boundary condition is applied in the simulation, and finite element method is used for solving the Poisson problem. This modality can be used as an accurate physical model to predict the distribution of electric fields in the brain generated by TTFields medical devices. Numerical results are obtained for a three-dimensional true human brain model.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Balanced-to-Unbalanced Bagley Power Divider with Wideband Common-Mode Suppression
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel miniaturized balanced-to-unbalanced (BTU) Bagley power divider with wideband common-mode (CM) suppression is proposed in this paper. The quarter-wavelength transformer can be replaced with a equivalent stub-loaded transmission line to realize the miniaturization effectively. Excellent wideband CM suppression can be achieved by using double-sided parallel-strip line 180° phase inverting structure. The operating frequency of the fabricated BTU Bagley power divider is located at 1.0 GHz with a miniaturized circuit size and the 6-dB fractional bandwidth is 70% from 0.5 GHz to 1.2 GHz. Furthermore, the CM suppression is better than 20 dB from 0.5 GHz to 1.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Dispersion Analysis of Ultrathin Grating for Free-Electron-Driven Frequency Comb
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The utility of free-electron radiation spans numerous fields, including biological imaging, particle detection, and light generation across a wide frequency range, from microwave to X-ray. Despite extensive efforts to manipulate properties such as directionality, phase, and polarization using metamaterials, the intrinsic broadband spectra of free-electron radiation have yet to be fully exploited for the generation of frequency combs, which represent state-of-the-art technology in metrology and spectroscopy. In this study, we demonstrate the analysis of the dispersion of ultrathin grating for the generation of a free-electron-driven frequency comb. By assuming the decay rate of arbitrary mode is the same in all directions of the designed structure, a rational and adaptable platform for generating a specific frequency comb is presented, which has the potential to advance the development of metrology and spectroscopy in the terahertz band.

articleTitle: Design of an Unvisualized Automotive Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: At present, most of the car antennas are metal antennas, which affect the beauty and occupy a lot of equipment space. In recent years, domestic and international academic research on the design of transparent glass antennas has made some progress. Based on the powerful antenna design function of HFSS, this paper simulates and designs a millimeter wave microstrip patch antenna based on quartz glass as the substrate, using ITO film as the ground plate and radiation patch, and the final antenna works at 2.45GHz (ISM band) with the optimized S11 of-21. 29dB, the highest in-band gain of 5.59dBi, and the light transmission rate can reach 80%.

articleTitle: Enhanced Second-Harmonic Generation Driven by Dual-Quasi Bound States in the Continuum
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Bound state in the continuum (BIC) is a dark mode with infinitely high quality factors(Q-factors), it has recently attracted considerable research attention in photonics. Here, we present a metasurface that can support two BICs, which consists of AlGaAs. By breaking the structural symmetry, the two BICs are transformed into quasi-bic modes because they are not protected by the symmetry. Furthermore, it is found that the two quasi-BICs resonate near the fundamental and the second harmonic respectively, which can be used to enhance efficiency of second harmonic generation. By exploiting the high Q characteristics of this structure at both frequencies, we can obtain a second harmonic generation efficiency of nearly 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with 1GW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>of pump intensity. Our proposed metasurface will offer good prospects for nonlinear operation.

articleTitle: A Wideband ME Dipole Array with Stable Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A low-profile wideband magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna array with stable gain is designed in this paper. First, the proposed ME dipole element realizes a wide bandwidth from 5.08 to 7.24 GHz (2.06 GHz, 33.4%), which exhibits two resonant modes. The microstrip line on the lower substrate is used to feed the slot and the three pair of dipoles on the upper substrate. Two rows of via connect the dipoles to the ground. Then, 1×4 ME dipole elements are used to construct the antenna array for high gain. The antenna array shows an impedance bandwidth (IMBW) of 5.1-7.07 GHz (1.97 GHz, 32.5%), with a stable gain from 10.8 dBi to 11.8 dBi. It is worth noting that the antenna profile height is only 0.08 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex>.

articleTitle: ISGW Characteristic Impedance Calculation Based on Conformal Mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide (ISGW) is a newly proposed planar waveguide, which has the characteristics of low loss, easy integration and self-encapsulation, and is especially suitable for millimeter wave systems. Related waveguides have been widely used in the research and design of millimeter wave devices and antennas. However, no theoretical study has been made on the propagation characteristics of the waveguide, such as dispersion and characteristic impedance. Therefore, this paper will use conformal mapping method to study the characteristic impedance of ISGW waveguide.

articleTitle: Diffractive Deep Neural Network for Microwave Imaging Based on a Multi-Layer Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this study, we designed a diffractive deep neural network (D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN) structure using a multi-layer transmitarray antenna. Each transmitarray surface is treated as a physical neural network (NN) layer, with each element representing a neuron. The interaction between electromagnetic (EM) waves and transmitarray surfaces can be regarded as the computation of NNs. The proposed D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN is applied for microwave imaging of the metal targets. Numerical results demonstrate that D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN can provide reliable imaging with good similarity to the target in terms of size, shape, and position.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on Low Pressure Discharge of Microwave Stepped Impedance Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The transient process of low-pressure air discharge in microwave stepped impedance transformer is described using three-dimensional (3D) spectral-element time-domain (SETD) method. The self-consistent coupling of electron fluid equation and Maxwell's equations is used to describe the electromagnetic-plasma system. The evolution of spatial distributions of discharge is obtained. The mechanism of low-pressure discharge is analyzed and explained. As time goes on, the electron distribution hot spot gathers toward the source end in the y-z plane. With the increase of the pressure, the electromagnetic field can be transmitted to the right side gradually, and the trend of electron density gathering to the incident side of the incident wave is weakened. Our research is beneficial to improve the matching performance of stepped impedance transformer.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Topological Gap Waveguide Based on Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The efficient backscatter suppression and robust transmission properties of photonic topological insulators (PTIs) promise to be a platform for high-performance microwave/millimeter-wave device design. In this paper, a reconfigurable gap waveguide (GW) is designed based on PTIs and its energy transfer tunable characteristics are realized using the anisotropic tunability of liquid crystals (LCs). This topological gap waveguide not only overcomes the problem of backscattering losses caused by manufacturing errors and structural bending in conventional gap waveguides, but is also compatible with conventional semiconductor technology. The proposed structure has potential applications in the backscatter suppression of tunable on-chip integrated topological photonic devices.

articleTitle: LSTM-Based Method for Characteristic Mode Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Characteristic mode (CM) theory has been widely used for antenna design and scattering problems. However, it is always challenging to correctly track the eigenmodes for complicated structures over a wide frequency band. Due to the typical time-series features of the mode data, a method based on long short-term memory neural network (LSTM) is proposed for mode tracking. Different modes at each frequency are distinguished and classified by learning the internal features between the mode data, which can overcome the mode degradation problem and thus achieve good tracking performance. The proposed method is validated by a U-slot patch antenna.

articleTitle: Large-Angle Phase/Frequency Scanned Ridge Waveguide Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a ridge waveguide slit phase-frequency sweep antenna array, the array consists of 10 heterogeneous ridge waveguides, the single waveguide unit adopts S-shaped slow wave line structure, the slit is opened on both sides of the center line of the broadside of the waveguide, the Taylor line source synthesis method is used to assign the antenna directional map, reduce the sub-flap level, and can reduce the beam width to ensure the signal transmission distance and transmission quality. The 3D simulation software is used to model and simulate the slit antenna. The simulation results show that the sub-flap level of the antenna is less than -18dB in the frequency band of 15.5GHz-16.5GHz, the azimuthal phase scan beam range is more than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{45}^{\circ}$</tex>, and the pitch frequency scan beam range is more than 50°. The antenna has a large frequency sweep range, easy processing and excellent performance, and can be used for airborne electric scanning radar or civil maritime navigation radar.

articleTitle: RCS Prediction of a Target Based on the Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper is based on the decision tree method in machine learning to predict the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of a complex target, where the original samples are simulated by using the Shooting and Bouncing Rays (SBR) method. The prediction method achieves good results and alleviates the problem of traditional RCS computation being time-consuming and expensive. A series of experimental analyses have been conducted on missile and ship targets to evaluate the accuracy and effectiveness of the RCS prediction model. The results demonstrate that the decision tree method based on machine learning is effective to predict the RCS of a target.

articleTitle: Simulation and Characteristics Analysis of Sea Surface Echoes Based on Actual Radar Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to simulate rough sea surface radar echoes based on actual radar signals. Firstly, the shooting and bouncing rays method is combined with two scale model (SBR-TSM) to calculate the EM scattering of the marine scene. Then the SBR-TSM method is accelerated with NVIDIA's Computational Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) and OptiX, which can greatly improve the efficiency of ray tracing while ensuring accuracy. Secondly, the scattering model is applied to each sea facet. The echo of linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal from each facet are summarized together in time frequency to synthesize the total radar echo. Then the total radar echo signal is processed with pulse compression to obtain sea clutter signals at different moments. Finally, the radar signal processing method is used to analyze the time domain, frequency domain and time-frequency domain characteristics of simulated rough sea surface echo data.

articleTitle: Protection Performance Test of HEMP Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper uses the pulse current injection (PCI) method to test the protection performance of six power line filters against high-altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HEMP). HEMP is injected into their incoming lines and the residual currents data of the corresponding outgoing lines are collected. The collected data is compared by 3 aspects including residual current peak, current rejection ratio and residual current waveform. The test results show that the peak value of residual current is less than 10 Amps(A) when the peak value of injection current of HEMP is 100 A, 500 A, 1000 A, 1800 A and 2500 A. The residual current peak and current suppression ratio are related to injection current peak. The test results provide reference for the protection performance test of HEMP filter.

articleTitle: Effect of Ionospheric Electron Density Model on Loran C Sky Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the difference of amplitude and time delay of Loran C sky wave are analyzed when different models are used to predict the electron density in the D region of the ionosphere. The simulation results show that when the incident angle is 80°, the difference of reflected signal amplitude between different models is 7dB, and the time delay is 2.15 μs.

articleTitle: Research on 3D Imaging of Unmanned Vehicle Ground Penetrating Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: By using the motion control parameters of the unmanned vehicle, the measurement information of the positioning auxiliary modules such as angle sensor, GPS and panoramic laser radar is fused, and the accurate loop scanning motion control of the vehicle is realized. The starting position of the loop scanning data measured by ground penetrating radar is calibrated, and the three-dimensional images of the indoor hidden structure and the underground structure of the road are obtained.

Author Keywords: Three dimensional imaging of ground penetrating radar

articleTitle: Application of Advanced MOR-Based Self-Adjoint EM Sensitivity Analysis for a Wideband Hybrid Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents the latest advances in the fast analysis method of electromagnetic (EM) sensitivity. EM sensitivity plays an important role in EM optimization, so how to obtain the sensitivity information faster has become the key to accelerating EM optimization. Applying the model order reduction (MOR) technique can significantly speed up the process of solving the large linear system. A MOR-based EM sensitivity analysis method has been applied to achieve faster sensitivity analysis. Besides, the formulation of this method is compatible with multiple MOR techniques. A wideband hybrid waveguide filter has been chosen to perform EM sensitivity analysis by applying this sensitivity analysis method.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Integrated Circularly Polarized Tightly Coupled Array Antenna Using Sequential Rotation Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces an ultra-wideband (UWB) integrated circularly polarized (CP) tightly coupled array (TCA) antenna using sequential rotation technology. The ultra-wide impedance matching property is realized by the TCA technology. And the sequential rotation technology uses 90° phase different feed to improve the axial ratio (AR). The combination of the two technologies can achieve an UWB CP array antenna. The final results show that the antenna can achieve ultra-wideband CP radiation from 6.97-18.69 GHz with AR < 3dB and VSWR < 3. Moreover, the TCA is designed in an integrated way, which makes its size very small.

articleTitle: A Discontinous Galerkin Integral Equation Method for Surface-Wire Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The surface-wire integral method is an efficient and versatile tool for analyzing electromagnetic radiation and scattering problems involving thin wires and arbitrarily shaped bodies. However, the conformal mesh for structures with dense surface-wire junctions can be challenging to generate and results in a large number of unknowns. In this letter, the implementation of the discontinuous Galerkin integral equation (DGIE) for surface-wire structure so that mesh generation for surfaces and wires is performed individually is reported. The formulation to evaluate the interaction of specially defined basis functions is presented in the DGIE framework. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method can reduce the unknown numbers and mesh flexibly, which can improve computational efficiency without losing accuracy.

articleTitle: A Near-Field Focused Conformal Antenna Array for Focused Microwave Head Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Microwave hyperthermia is an emerging medical technology that diagnoses and treats cancer based on microwave heat effects and biological effects. A near-field focused conformal antenna array is proposed for focused microwave head hyperthermia. The proposed array is formed of 2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 4$</tex> microstrip antennas, and the spatial distributions of all array elements fit well with the helmet-shaped microwave hyperthermia chamber. With differential evolution algorithm applied, the excitation weights of the antenna elements are optimized so that the electromagnetic wave radiated by the conformal antenna array can be focused at the desired position inside the helmet-shaped chamber. Full-wave simulation verifies the feasibility of the near-field focused conformal antenna for microwave hyperthermia.

articleTitle: A Bandstop Filter Based on Modified Defected Ground Structure with Compact Size
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper reports a compact size bandstop filter using Defected Ground Structure (DGS). The proposed filter consists of squared shaped defect and U-shaped defect sticked on the ground plane. This design is based on a parallel LC circuit model and designed to work at 1 GHz. The filter is implemented on a FR-4 dielectric plate and its size is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.049\lambda_{g}\times 0.049\lambda_{g}$</tex> (where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{g}$</tex> is the wavelength in waveguide).

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of AlGaN/GaN Heterostructure Based on Spectral-Element Time-Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To describe the electrical characteristics of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs, this paper adopts the spectral-element time-domain (SETD) method to simulate the AlGaN/GaN HEMT devices. The boundary condition of heterojunction is introduced into the drift diffusion model to obtain the volt-ampere characteristic of AlGaN/GaN HEMT. The numerical results are compared with the commercial software COMSOL simulation results to verify the accuracy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An IGBT Desaturation Protection Technique With Leading Edge Blanking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: IGBTis a prevalent power device that has been widely employed in the industrial domain. During operation, IGBT often encounters faults such as short circuits, which would cause damage to the IGBT if it remains in a short-circuit state for an extended period, thus adversely affecting the operation of industrial systems. The paper proposes an IGBT desaturation protection technique with leading edge blanking, which monitors the occurrence of short circuits in IGBT and provides timely protection. The leading edge blanking technique ensures that the IGBT has enough time to enter the saturation region during conduction, thereby minimizing the possibility of erroneous detection. The proposed desaturation protection technique is designed based on SMIC 0.18um BCD process. According to simulation results, the leading edge blanking time is 310 ns, the desaturation detection charging current is 523 uA, and the desaturation reference voltage is 8.95 V.

articleTitle: Electro-Thermal Simulation of GaN HEMT by Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: High power dissipation in the Gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor (GaN HEMT) leads to severe self heating effects, resulting in performance degradation. This study presents a comprehensive numerical electro-thermal simulation method of GaN HEMT by self-consistently solving the drift diffusion transport equations and thermal conduction equation with various temperature-dependent parameters, including band gap and electron mobility. According to simulation results, the self-heating effects significantly degrade device performance.

Author Keywords: gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor (GaN HEMT)

articleTitle: A Hybrid Scattering Center Modeling Method for Composite Scene
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach that utilizes SAR images and CAD models to effectively model the scattering centers of composite scenes. The method involves establishing the environmental scattering center using pixel information from existing SAR images and electromagnetic algorithm calibration, while the target scattering center is established based on a CAD model of the target. To assess the accuracy of our method, we conducted simulations of the scattering fields for the Suez Canal and a freighter. The results were then compared with both the measured data and the results obtained through physical optics (PO) simulations, demonstrating a remarkable similarity of above 81.20%.

articleTitle: Synergistic Effects Simulation of MOSFET by Control Volume Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The synergistic effects of the electromagnetic pluse (EMP) and analog transient radiation effects in electronics (ATREE) are numerically investigated by our In-house Solver. The drift-diffusion model is discretized by control volume finite element method. Numerical results of metal oxide semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) indicate that the current distur-bance by EMP is noticeable in the time range about 10-100ns. Moreover, the amplitudes of drain current increases obviously with the increasing transient dose rate.

Author Keywords: Analog transient radiation effects in electronics (ATREE)

articleTitle: Response of NMOS to Combined Ionization and EMP Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Electronic systems in space or nuclear devices are exposed to both ionizing radiation and electromagnetic radiation environments. Experimental results have indicated that the semiconductor devices may suffer severe damage in the combined environment of ionizing radiation and electromagnetic radiation. In this work, a total ionizing dose (TID) effects and electromagnetic pulses (EMP) combined effect model of NMOS device is established. Simulation results show that the NMOS will exhibit more severe leakage current increase and sub-threshold characteristics degradation in the combined environments.

articleTitle: Optical Selective Transmission Properites of Annular Aperture Array
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Annular Aperture Arrays (AAA) structure is one of the grating structures, having the property of enhanced optical transmission (EOT). In this paper, we have established integral equations for two-dimensional periodic structures to calculate the propagation properties of electromagnetic wave in the AAA structure.

articleTitle: Design and Validation of Single-Layer Evanescent Wave Absorber in Rectangular Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, for absorbing waves below the cutoff frequency of a rectangular waveguide (RWG), i.e., absorb the evanescent waves (EWs), a single-layer EW absorber with an ideal lossy capacitive metasurface (LCMS) is proposed. Based on the principle of momentum matching, the working mechanism is analyzed. Prototype is fabricated for validation, and the maximum measured absorptance reaches 97%. The EW absorber provide a new approach to reduce electromagnetic interference (EMI) caused by the evanescent modes in small metallic cavities and near-field of integrated circuits (ICs).

articleTitle: Design of a W-band Low Phase Noise VCO with Colpitts Topology in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces the design of a W-band voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), which achieves very low phase noise and excellent figure of merit (FOM) at 1-MHz offset. The circuit is based on the Colpitts topology structure. The VCO is configured to operate at a fundamental frequency of 47 GHz and utilizes second harmonic extraction for output. Load pulling technique is employed at the output stage to achieve maximum output power. The VCO tank is set to the optimal capacitance ratio to ensure the lowest phase noise, which aligns closely with theoretical expectations. In addition, the combination of tail current noise optimization and resonant network filtering techniques is also used to improve phase noise. The circuit is designed using the 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS process. The designed area is only 0.06 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>excluding pads. The VCO outputs a frequency range from 90 to 97 GHz. The phase noise at a 1-MHz offset is -101.5 dBc/Hz. With a voltage supply of 2.5V, the power consumption is 30 mW. The FoM at 1-MHz offset is -184.7 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: A Low Reflection Loss 1-Bit Element for Reconfigurable Reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we present a 1-bit reconfigurable reflectarray element with low reflection loss. The proposed element consists of three substrate layers and a single PIN diode to realize reconfigurable performance. A radiating patch is printed on the top layer, and a slot is etched on the ground plane in the middle layer, where a PIN diode is loaded on the slot. By reducing the current flowing through the PIN diode, lower reflection loss is achieved in this work. The reflection loss of the proposed element is within 0.1 dB in both ON and OFF states of the PIN diode in the frequency range of 5 to 6.6GHz. Two phase states with a phase difference of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$180^{\circ}\pm 20^{\circ}$</tex> are realized from 5.2 to 6.36GHz.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Filtering Antenna with Parasitic Patches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A high-gain circularly polarized (CP) filtering antenna with parasitic patches is designed without additional filtering structure. The lower radiation patch is composed of a pair of parasitic patches, truncated-corner square patch and microstrip feeding line, and the truncated square patch realizes the main CP radiation. The crossed slot is etched on the upper stacked patch to generate high-frequency band radiation null, and the low-frequency band radiation null is generated from the microstrip feeding line at the lower patch. Simulation results illustrate that the proposed antenna can generate 19.33% (2.15-2.61 GHz) impedance bandwidth, 5.54% (2.28-2.41 GHz) axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and about 8.4 dBi realized gain.

articleTitle: Characterization of Near-Field Coupling With Unshielded Star-Quad Cable Above a Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A transmission-line model for characterizing near-field coupling with a star quad cable is improved, where it utilizes a pair of electric and magnetic dipole moments for reproducing the near field distributions. The induced common- and differential-mode currents at balanced terminals of the star-quad cable are predicted by using the transmission line theory. The obtained results are in good agreement with those generated by the commercial software FEKO. Further, we pay attention to such star-quad cables having four conductors arranged in a balanced geometry, providing immunity to an external coupling. It is shown that the star-quad cable has very good advantage in suppressing electromagnetic interferences, as compared to twisted-wire pair cables.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Metasurface Antenna for Search and Rescue Radar Transponder
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A circularly polarized metasurface antenna for search and rescue radar transponder (SART) is designed and discussed in this paper. The antenna is a double-layer structure with metasurface radiation patch, ground floor and microstrip line loaded on two layers of substrate respectively. The circular polarization design of the metasurface structure is carried out using the characteristic mode theory. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna can work well in the SART working band (9.2GHz-9.5GHz) and realize circular polarization.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Domain Constraint Enhanced VBIM for Multi-Scale Contrast Objects Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A robust hierarchical domain constraint (HDC) strategy is proposed to enhance the VBIM for the multiscale contrast objects reconstruction in this paper. During the iterations of VBIM-HDC, with the classification of background and scatterers cells, the parameters of the background cells are set as the same as the actual background and removed from the inversion. The major work of the VBIM-HDC is to divide the inversion process into several stages, and the classification of cells is evaluated separately at each stage, making the classification reversible. And the HDC can effectively classify the inversion domain of low-contrast objects without negligence in the multiscale contrast objects case, as well as the continuously varying inhomogeneous objects' low-contrast parts. Another advantage of HDC is the threshold determining the classification of cells can be flexibly chosen. This robust constraint of the inversion domain compresses the solution space so that the ill-posedness of the inverse problem is mitigated, and better accuracy thus is achieved. Numerical results validate the accuracy, and robustness of the proposed VBIM-HDC.

articleTitle: A Nodal DGTD Method Based on Damped Purely Hyperbolic Maxwell Equation System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper establishes an electromagnetic solver based on the nodal discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (NDGTD) method with consideration of divergence correction. Firstly, divergence-cleaning method is used to enforce Gauss's laws. With the auxiliary variables and the damping terms, the damped pure hyperbolic Maxwell's equation (DPHM) system has been established. The numerical governing equations corresponding to the DPHM have been formulated in the framework of the NDGTD. Numerical examples have been presented to verify the effectiveness of the NDGTD-DPHM method.

articleTitle: Enhanced Efficiency for DGTD Simulations with Frozen Element Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a frozen element strategy (FES) for the Discontinuous Galerkin Time Domain (DGTD) method. The strategy involves freezing elements in the source-free region where the electromagnetic fieldvalues are zero. By employing this method, we have achieved significant computational savings during the early stages of time-step iterations, while almost maintaining the same level of accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the efficiency enhancement and accuracy of our approach.

articleTitle: A Fast FDTD Grid Generation Method and its Application in Scattering Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a fast FDTD grid generation method and it can efficiently calculates the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of targets. The method reconstructs the mesh by extracting information from the triangular surface elements of the stl file. It is compared with the MoM method and is found to significantly reduce the calculation time for irregular models such as aircraft, ships, and rockets, etc. Through two example, including accuracy and computation time comparisons, it can be concluded that the proposed method offers a reasonable level of precision while significantly reducing calculation time.

articleTitle: Multimode Vortex Electromagnetic Antenna and its Communication Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A multimode vortex electromagnetic antenna for communication application is designed and implemented, which works in 5.5-6.1GHz. The antenna can generate multimode vortex electromagnetic wave, and the isolation and reflection coefficient are below -50dB and -10dB in the frequency band, respectively. The multimode communication experiment is carried out, the results show that multimode vortex electromagnetic antenna is suitable for communication and is an alternative solution for high-performance communications.

articleTitle: Design of Ka-Band Broadband Millimeter-Wave Antenna Based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband millimeter-wave antenna based on a metasurface is proposed. The impedance bandwidth of this antenna can be greatly widened by cutting the corners and slotting the conventional microstrip antenna and loading a double-loop metasurface on top of it. The 10-dB bandwidth of this broadband millimeter-wave antenna based on the metasurface structure is 24.41 - 40.86 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of 50.4 %. in the whole working bandwidth, the gain of the antenna is greater than 4 dB, and the highest in-band gain is 8.5 dB. The overall size of the antenna is 8 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 8$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 1.14$</tex> mm.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis of Coupled Scattering Mechanism of Creeping Waves in Complex Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper investigates the contribution of multiple coupling effects caused by creeping waves in the scattering characteristics of complex targets. Firstly, ray tracing was conducted on the creeping waves on the surface of complex targets. Compared to previous studies that only explored the propagation path of the creeping waves, this paper additionally examined the spatial trajectory of the radiation rays emitted by the creeping waves, focusing on the reflection process of the radiation rays. After clarifying the ray path of the creeping-reflection coupling mechanism, this paper combines UTD with GO to analyze the scattering field of this coupling mechanism, and provides a calculation method. Through the examples in this paper, it can be seen that the simulation of target characteristics, taking the creeping waves and their coupling effects into account, expands and completes the types of scattering mechanisms, and more realistically reflects the radar target characteristics of complex targets.

articleTitle: An Accelerated TD-NFPO Method for Computing Near-Field Scattering of a Parabolic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To address the issue of computational time in near-field scattering analysis of electrically large scatterers, a time-domain near-field physical optics (TD-NFPO) method based on spatial symmetry is proposed. This method is employed to compute the temporal near-field scattering signals along the axis of symmetry of a parabolic surface. Based on the theoretical formulation of the TD-NFPO, it is derived that the total scattered field of a parabolic structure is four times that of its 1/4-section scattering field. The efficiency and accuracy of this method are validated through numerical experiments. The accelerated TD-NFPO method based on the high-frequency approximation algorithm is well suited for the near-field time-domain scattering analysis of large-aperture parabolic antennas, providing some assistance in electromagnetic compatibility issues for radio telescopes.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Coherent Registration Algorithm for High-Speed Target Under System Error
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In the field of multi-band fusion imaging, multi-band coherent registration will directly affect the final imaging result. In this paper, the influence of incoherent factors such as target velocity and system error on the high resolution range profile(HRRP) is quantitatively analyzed. Aiming at solving the distortion problem of HRRP, based on image entropy and compressed sensing theory, velocity compensation algorithm and system error compensation algorithm are designed to compensate the additional phases generated by incoherent factors, which restore the real HRRP and make lower and upper bands achieve coherence. Simulation verifies the effectiveness of the compensation algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimization of Sparse Planar Arrays using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper uses genetic algorithm for sparse layout optimization of square array and concentric ring array to verify the feasibility of using genetic algorithm to optimize sparse layout array, and compares the impact of four different array element layout methods on the maximum sidelobe level of the optimized antenna pattern.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Absorber with Reconfigurable Units
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A broadband absorber with reconfigurable unit is presented in this paper. With the varactor diodes loaded, this absorber can achieve four reconfigurable absorbing performance at low-frequency, combined with a broadband absorbing structure, the ultra-wideband absorbing performance is realized in the range of 0.5 GHz to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Valley-Hall Photonic Topological Insulators in Microstrip Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Electromagnetic System Topological Robust Waveguides (ESTRW) have been extensively studied due to their robust transmission characteristics, which make them immune to defects. In this paper, we propose a grounded planar valley-Hall photonic topological insulator based on the photon topological theory. We demonstrate efficient conversion from classical metal transmission lines to topological waveguides and verify the robust transmission of the waveguide.

articleTitle: Design of an eleven-way power divider for cosecant-squared beamforming
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: According to the requirements of the cosecant-squared-shaped beam of a secondary surveillance radar antenna, a genetic algorithm is used to optimize the amplitude and phase of the antenna elements. Based on the optimization results, this paper proposes an unequal eleven-way microstrip power divider. Connect the power divider to the antenna for verification, and the resulting beam matches the specified cosecant-squared-shaped beam.

articleTitle: A Compact MIMO Antenna with Frequency Selective Surface Cells for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-band MIMO antenna for Sub-6G communication is proposed. Two operating bands are generated by the combination of two rectangular frame structures of different sizes. In addition, by designing and loading frequency selective surface cells and then arranging them appropriately, the antenna is miniaturized to improve the isolation of the antenna while ensuring a compact structure. The results show that the -10dB return loss bandwidth of the antenna is 3.38-3.58GHz and 4.43-6.30GHz, which can cover the n78 and n79 bands in 5G communication. Furthermore, the antenna has good radiation and diversity characteristics with the isolation less than -15dB in the operating band.

articleTitle: Study on Radio Wave Coverage Along the Railway Containing Multi-Tunnel Entrance Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Radio wave coverage in a mixed scenario containing multi-tunnel environment along railway is studied in this paper. The scenario specifically includes three typical environments: open space, confined space, and open-confined space. The main research of this paper is on the radio wave coverage along a route passing through two tunnel entrances. Due to the complex environment considered, finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method is used to model and analyze the radio wave coverage of a Yagi antenna. The results indicate that reducing the open space distance, decreasing the antenna installation height within the safe height range, and installing the antenna near the horizontal center while keeping the antenna height unchanged, can provide smoother radio wave coverage along the tunnel entrance.

articleTitle: High-Quality Sampling Inverse Design Scheme with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Artificial intelligence techniques are being used for the inverse design of microwave devices, but challenges such as high computation cost, high-dimensional data, non-uniformity, and low-quality samples in design space can negatively affect modeling performance. To overcome these challenges, a highquality sampling inverse design scheme deep learning method (HQS-DL) is proposed for automated microwave filter design. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) is used for forward simulationbased sampling to tentatively select high-quality samples, and multilabel synthetic minority over-sampling technique (MLSMOTE) is utilized to enlarge the training samples and make them more uniform. A neural network is used to efficiently represent the nonlinear mapping between input S-parameters and required filter structural parameters. The proposed method is verified with a band-pass microstrip hairpin filter and achieves better modeling effectiveness and inverse design efficiency than conventional methods, enabling quick prediction of device parameters for different center frequencies and bandwidths.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-Band Dual-Sense Circularly Polarized DRA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile dual band dual polarized DRA is proposed. In the lower band, the dielectric resonator (DR) is excited by the cross slots etched on the ground plane fed by a microstrip line under the substrate, and the left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) is controlled by the cross slots, and the profile is reduced by the air vias etched in the DR. In the upper band, the four DRs arranged counterclockwise around the center are excited by the rectangle slots in the ground plane, which is fed by a one-quarter Wilkinson power divider with a 90° phase difference for each port and the right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) is attained. The simulated results achieve an available bandwidth of 15.4% (2.41-2.81GHz) in the lower band and 31.5% (2.97-4.08GHz) in the upper band with a profile of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.11 \lambda$</tex>.

articleTitle: Low-RCS Low-Profile Patch Antenna Using Polarization Conversion Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A dumbbell shaped novel wideband polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) is proposed for use on patch antenna to reduce radar cross section (RCS). The metasurface (MS) composed of rectangle and two pairs of irregular hexagons realizes line-to-line polarization conversion from 7.7 GHz to 18.8 GHz with polarization conversion rate (PCR) higher than 90%. When the PCM and its orthogonal elements are coplanar arranged orderly around the radiating patch, the RCS of the antenna is significantly reduced by at least 6 dB in the entire X-band and Ku-band. The proposed antenna has a stable operation at 5.2 GHz, a low profile of 0.05 and the peak realized gain of 7.72 dBi. This antenna can be used for wireless communication in military environments.

articleTitle: EM Modeling of Substrate Integrated Waveguide Using a Fast Frequency Sweep Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The wide-band electromagnetic finite element modelling involves solving the matrix equations at a series of discretized frequency points. However, the wide-band modeling often leads to high computational costs. In this paper, a fast frequency sweeping approach based on the model order reduction (MOR) technique is proposed to analyze substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). For complex SIW structures, the fast frequency sweep approach can significantly reduce the computational costs based on a reduced model. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed method for the SIW simulations.

articleTitle: MIMO OTA Testing for 5G User Equipment Using Dynamic Channel Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The 2×2 and even 4×4 downlink MIMO are implemented more generally in 5G user equipments (UEs), the complexity of which poses great challenges to performance evaluation and test verification for 5G UEs. Given that the existing static channel models defined by 3GPP could not rank different UEs in terms of performance effectively, CTIA proposes the dynamic channel model with link adaptation accordingly for standardization. In this work, the first MIMO OTA testing system with dynamic channel model is integrated, based on which four 5G commercial UEs are tested. The measurement results and related analysis proves the good feasible and the ability to distinguish different UEs of the proposed dynamic channel model with link adaptation.

articleTitle: Power Amplifier on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: We have designed a power amplifier (PA) using an SSPP transmission line (TL). The impedance of the SSPP unit structure was calculated based on its equivalent circuit model and matched with the source and load impedance of the amplifier chip.
