To evaluate the accuracy of the model, it is applied to simulate the shielding effectiveness of a metal enclosure with a carbon fiber composite (CFC) door, the results of which are compared with experimental data. The comparison shows a good agreement, further demonstrating the accuracy of the embedded anisotropic thin layer model.

articleTitle: Radar Backscattering Characterization of Soil Surface: Comparisons between Backscattering Models and Indoor Microwave Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to explore the backscatter characteristics of bare soil, we conducted indoor microwave measurements, and compared the experimental results with surface backscattering model: Dubois and AIEM. The effects of surface parameters such as root mean square height, soil moisture content, and system parameters such as incident angle and polarization mode on radar microwave backscattering characteristics was analyzed, and revealed the law of radar backscattering coefficient changing with these parameters. The comparison with the surface models showed that when the RMS height is greater than 1 cm, the measured value have good consistency with AIEM, which indicates the great potential of the indoor microwave system in model verification.

articleTitle: A E-Band Receiver With 8.8dB Noise Figure in 55-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces an E-band receiver with an noise figure(NF) of 8.8dB. The low-noise amplifier using a multitransformer matching network reduces NF and increases the bias voltage of the mixer provided by the transimpedance amplifier(TIA) in the later stages and increases the mixing gain. The 63GHz-71GHz wideband receiver is realized under the 55nm CMOS process. The receiver has a conversion gain of 26.8dB, an NF of 8.8dB, and a 1dB compression point (P1dB) of −24dBm.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband MIMO Antenna with Shared Radiator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband 5G MIMO mobile antenna with a shared radiator is proposed. The working band range is 3.3-6.0GHz, covering n77, n78, n79 and WLAN 5G working bands, which can meet a large number of application scenarios of 5G mobile phones. In addition, the antenna is applied to self-decoupling, defect ground, direction diversity and other technologies and principles in the decoupling way, without the use of complex decoupling structure, to ensure that its structure is simple and easy to process, small size is suitable for today's 5G mobile phones.

articleTitle: Development of Isotropic Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, two antennas with isotropic radiation patterns are proposed. A cross-shaped dipole is conformed to the surface of a table tennis ball for isotropic radiation pattern. The gain variation over the far-field sphere is about 3.2 dB. Furthermore, an antenna with two cross-shaped dipoles is introduced. The two dipoles are printed on the two poles of the table tennis ball. The gain variation is less than 2 dB.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Susceptibility Test and Analysis of Brushless DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the development of electronic technology, the electromagnetic environment becomes more and more complex, leading to increasing importance of the anti-interference ability of electronic equipment. In this paper, a conductive susceptibility test platform was built, and the brushless DC motor was selected to be the device under test. This paper first introduces the working principle of the brushless DC motor. Then the conductive susceptibility of the motor is tested with the speed change as the sensitive phenomenon. Finally, the electromagnetic sensitive threshold and the susceptibility mechanism of the motor is analyzed through the test result.

articleTitle: Dual-mode Cavity Antenna with Filtering Response
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a compact filtering antenna is proposed at 26 GHz for millimeter wave applications. This antenna is composed of a full-metal cavity loaded with two symmetrical slots. By properly feed the antenna, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</inf> cavity mode and slot mode can be excited simultaneously, obtaining a dual-mode performance for wideband property. Besides, by adjusting the position of the slots, one radiation null can be well produced at upper stopband due to the coupling formed between the cavity mode and slot mode. Additionally, another radiation null is accompanied with TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">130</inf> mode, further improving the out-of-band rejection at upper stopband. Finally, the proposed antenna is fabricated by 3D printing technology, and the measured results agree well with the simulated ones. Measurement results show that a wide bandwidth of 21.6% covering from 23.6 to 29.3 GHz is obtained, with a maximum gain of 8.7 dBi. Besides, two radiation nulls can be well observed at upper stopband. The overall properties show that proposed antenna is a good candidate for millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: Source-Configured Microwave Plasmonic Vortices Based on Single Meta-Particle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, generation of plasmonic vortices with tunable topologic charges is proposed in the microwave regime. Tunable vortices with topologic charges of 0, +1 and -1 can be configured by illuminating incident plane waves with linearly polarization (LP), left-circularly polarization (LHCP) and right-circularly polarization (RHCP) on a single meta-particle, respectively. A spiral meta-particle operating at 2.94 GHz is designed, fabricated and measured to demonstrate the source-configured characteristics. The results showed that simulation and test are consistent with the theoretical ones.

articleTitle: A High Precision Ballistic Target Recognition Framework Using Multi-Subband Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a radar target recognition framework based on ultra-wideband (UWB) electromagnetic scattering features extracted from the fused full band. Firstly, multiple frequency subbands are fused to obtain UWB High Range Resolution Profile (HRRP) and parametric features based on geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) model of the target. Secondly, the UWB HRRP are fused with UWB parametric features by proposed target recognition framework. Thirdly, target recognition is accomplished with the proposed framework in which the concatenated features are set as the input of an existing network. Simulations results show the validity of our method and reveal that it can achieve better recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: On the Efficient Analysis of Antenna with High-$\kappa$ Dielectric Slabs Using Discontinuous Galerkin Integral Equations Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Using high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa$</tex> dielectrics or materials with high dielectric constants is increasingly popular in emerging antenna and microwave components. The electromagnetic analysis of them often encounters dense mesh and massive unknowns, which results in cumbersome simulation and optimization. To alleviate this difficulty, the discontinuous Galerkin surface integral equation (DG-SIE) and an independent mesh procedure are presented so that the metallic sheets attached to the dielectric surface are mesh independently for two sets of unknown currents. Two numerical examples, including a high dielectric constant array antenna and a frequency-selective structure, are carried out to verify that the proposed method can improve computational efficiency, reduce the number of unknowns and save computational resources while guaranteeing accuracy.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Frequency Selective Rectenna for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A rectenna with dual-band and dual-polarized for simultaneous Wireless information and power transfer is proposed. The proposed rectenna consists of a single-layer, dual-port MIMO antenna with a dual-band rectifying circuit. The dual-port MIMO antenna operates in two ports with a high frequency band overlap and a wide bandwidth. A dual-band rectifying circuit connected to one of the ports enables DC conversion in both operating bands by means of a frequency selective structure. Ultimately, the rectenna enables the simultaneous transmission of power and information in two different frequency bands 2.43-2.56 GHz and 3.88-4.43 GHz. where the highest rectification efficiency of 74.9% at frequency point 2.45 GHz and the highest rectification efficiency of 75.9 % at frequency point 4 GHz is achieved when the input power is 14 dBm.

Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: A Novel Tunable Temperature-Controlled VO2 Metasurface for Beam Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel tunable temperature-controlled vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) metasurface for beam regulation is proposed. The metasurface consists of non-tunable split-ring resonator and tunable VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-metal hybrid structure. Using the generalized Snell's law beam regulation method, the dynamic regulation of the reflected beam direction is realized based on the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> phase transition principle. The simulation results show that under the excitation of vertical incident plane wave at 0.75 THz, the angle of reflected wave can be dynamically switched between 0°, ±15°, and ±30° by changing the state of different phase transition temperatures VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> under fixed array through temperature control.

articleTitle: Wide-Beam Millimeter-Wave Circularly Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A wide-beam millimeter-wave circularly polarized (CP) magneto-electric dipole antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna inherits the advantages of simple structure and low cross polarization from the magneto-electric dipole antenna, mainly consisting of the magneto-electric dipole, metallic via, and split ring. The half-power beamwidth of the antenna is greatly enhanced by adding metallic vias around the magneto-electric dipole formed by two L-shaped patches. The antenna has a wide half-power beamwidth and a wide 3-dB axial ratio (AR) beamwidth, which is suitable for applications requiring a wide angle range for communication scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced DGTD Method Based on AVX Acceleration Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we presented a hardware acceleration technique that utilizes advanced vector extensions (AVX) instruction set to enhance the solution process of the discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method. Several examples were used to assess the performance improvement achieved by AVX-accelerated DGTD method. The results demonstrate significant enhancements in the performance of the DGTD method through the utilization of AVX instruction set.

articleTitle: Research on the Field-to-Wire Coupling of the Time Domain Hybrid Method in the Shielding Cavity Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper uses an efficient time domain hybrid method to solve the field-to-wire coupling problem. A transient co-simulation solver with a unidirectional irradiation type is utilized to simulate the response generated in parallel arrangements of different types of cables with equal length inside the electrically large-scale nacelle model. Through the analysis of the surface current distribution of the aircraft fuselage, the cause of the numerical oscillation of the electric field inside and outside the model, and the induction response of the cable, the results verify the ability of the hybrid algorithm to calculate the internal cables of the electrically large-scale model. In addition, experiments have shown that in order to reduce the impact of strong electromagnetic pulses on the normal operation of aircraft cables, better shielding effects can be achieved by improving the shielding capability of the aircraft fuselage, adjusting the wiring position of cables in the cabin, and using shielding layer structures for cables.

articleTitle: An Improved SBR-PTD Method for EM Scattering from Moving Target
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an improved hybrid method of shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) physical and theory of diffraction (PTD) method for the analysis of electromagnetic (EM) scattering from the moving target. Initially, geodetic coordinate system (GCS), the local coordinate system (LCS) of target, and projection coordinate system (PCS) are established. And the octree is built based on the LCS. Secondly, the target is converted to the PCS. The scanning line algorithm is employed for accelerating shadow elimination. Then, rays are transformed from GCS to the LCS of the target. The ray-marching method based on Octree is utilized to speed up the high-order ray tracing. Finally, the radar cross section (RCS) of our method is compared with those of the MLFMM and traditional SBR. The comparison demonstrates the efficiency of the presented method in the scattering analysis of the moving target.

articleTitle: A Spectrum Allocation Method for Avoiding Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the increasing number of RF electronic devices and the scarcity of spectrum resources, the issue of Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) has become increasingly severe. To address this problem, a spectrum allocation method based on the graph coloring algorithm is proposed. The method takes into account fairness in allocation by prioritizing spectrum resources for devices with weaker performance. Additionally, rounds and constraints are introduced to prevent the skewing of spectrum resources towards a single device, ensuring fairness in spectrum allocation. The proposed method provides a solution for efficient and fair spectrum allocation, mitigating the EMI challenges associated with the proliferation of RF electronic devices.

articleTitle: Active Integrated Antenna Based on Minimum Noise Matching
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, in order to discard the impedance matching circuit and reduce the antenna overall size, a directional antenna integrated a low noise amplifier (LNA) with ATF-54143 transistor is designed. Two 50ohm matching networks between the antenna and the LNA can be eliminated, and the insertion loss and the space occupation of RF front-end system have also been reduced. The simulated results show that this directional antenna with input impedance of 23.1-j15.4 ohm rather than 50 ohm at 2.45GHz and has a great radiation performance. The noise figure of the integrated antenna decreases by 0.1 at 2.45GHz, in comparison with the traditional cascade circuit by designing 50ohm matching networks. It provides a useful guiding method for the design of active antennas.

articleTitle: Radiation and Shielding of 5G Smart Phones
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The power of 5G smart phones is measured in frequency domain with electromagnetic spectrum analyzer. The measured power of China Unicom, China Telecom and China Mobile at the operating frequency is −50dBm, −52dBm and −45dBm respectively. The measured power of China Unicom, China Telecom and China Mobile after opening the shielding device is −43dBm, −41dBm and −36dBm respectively. The results of the measurement showed that the 5G signals of the three operators were completely shielded by signal Shielding device.

articleTitle: Beam Steering for Array Antenna Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an algorithm based on deep learning for beam steering with an array antenna. Array factors are often used for beam steering problems, but because array factors cannot handle coupling influence between array antenna elements and edge effect, A deep neural network is designed to learn the physics of beam steering from data computed by array factor (AF) theory and the active element pattern (AEP). Putting the phases predicted by neural network and phases predicted by AF into simulated software to compare the main lobe direction. The results show that the trained deep neural network's output phases fulfilling the input main lobe direction requirement and it takes the coupling influence between array antenna elements into account.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Filter Method Based on Dual Sensors for Spatial Magnetic Noise Suppression
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An adaptive filter method based on dual sensors for spatial magnetic noise suppression is proposed. Based on normalized-least-mean-square(NLMS) algorithm, an adaptive filter model of spatial magnetic noise is established. The results show that the magnetic noise is suppressed while the SNR in frequency domain of the weak low frequency target magnetic signal is improved.

articleTitle: Full-Space Beam Scanning Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a full-space beam scanning antenna based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is proposed. The proposed antenna is composed of a SSPPs loaded by the varactor diodes and periodic metallic patches. The periodic patches can transform the slow waves from SSPPs into fast waves, and the cutoff frequency can be reconfigured by changing the capacitance of the varactor diode, which will make the radiation angle of the beam change within a fixed frequency. Simulation results show that the radiation angle ranges from −90° to 90° at 9 GHz.

articleTitle: Study on the Causes of HPM Spurious Out-of-band Emissions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The HPM signal source is usually affected by a number of factors such as equipment and measurement environment, which results in the different between the measured HPM and the ideal HPM. This leads to the possibility of other out-of-band emissions in the frequency domain, which can have a significant impact on subsequent simulations and other work. In this paper, we change the perturbation mode of the carrier frequency in the fitted HPM. The result is found that the out-of-band emissions might generate when the amplitude fluctute randomly in a certain continuous time. The amplitude of carrier fluctuations, the start time and duration of carrier disturbance do not affect the out-of-band emissions.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband Droplet-Shaped Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna for VHF/UHF Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized broadband droplet-shaped pattern-reconfigurable antenna working at very high frequency (VHF) band and ultra-high frequency band (UHF) is proposed. The antenna size is significantly reduced by meandering the top-loaded metal strip, and the impedance bandwidth is broadened by loading passive lumped element on the radiating elements. The overall dimension of the proposed antenna is 0.182λ×0.066λ at the lowest operating frequency. The antenna shows a well-match frequency response with voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) less than 2.5 from 110 MHz to 661 MHz (142.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). A four-element square array is constructed by rotating each single element 90 degree around the center. The radiation pattern reconfigurable function is successfully realized, which covers four directions in the azimuth plane.

articleTitle: Switchable Absorptive Frequency-Selective Reflector/Absorber with Wide AbsorptionBands
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a switchable absorptive frequency-selective reflector (AFSR)/absorber with wide absorption bands. Two lossy dipoles are used in the unit cell to absorb the electromagnetic (EM) waves at low- and high-frequencies, while transmit EM waves between the two absorption bands. A lumped resistor is welded on a strip line to absorb the EM waves between the two absorption bands. In order to achieve switchable performance, the ideal PIN diodes are welded on both sides of the resistor. Under the primary polarization incident EM waves, the structure operates as an AFSR when the diode is turned off or as an absorber when the diode is turned on while it is transparent to the orthogonal polarization incident EM waves. The proposed switchable AFSR/absorber has the potential for multi-polarized antenna system, as it will not affect the normal operation of the orthogonal polarized antenna. A dipole is studied based on the proposed AFSS, it has improved radiation performance and better stealth performance.

articleTitle: Design of a Spherical Phased Array Based on Broadband Circularly Polarized Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The spherical conformal array is of great interest to researchers because of its full-space scanning capability. However, to achieve excellent performance of beam scanning, the number of units to be motivated needs to be controlled. When all units are motivated simultaneously, there are some units whose maximum radiation direction is opposite to the beam scanning direction, so the back-lobe and side-lobe of the pattern raise and cause the deterioration of gain. In this paper, we propose to apply the broadband circularly polarized dipole antenna to the large-scale spherical conformal array and obtain excellent beam scanning performance by calculating the effective excitation areas. It can be applied to satellite communication, radar reconnaissance and other fields in practical engineering.

articleTitle: A High Performance Microcavity Filter for Mobile Communication Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an eight-cavity filter for B34 and B39 mobile frequency bands is designed, the operating frequency is 1.885GHz-2.025GHz (S11<-14dB), the maximum insertion loss in the pass band is 0.62, and the minimum insertion loss is 0.34. At 70MHz out-of-band, out-of-band rejection is greater than 80dB. The overall size is 47.6mm×23.2mm×9mm, the microcavity filter proposed in this paper, by changing the conventional topology and the size of the metal probe, makes the device have the characteristics of miniaturization, high stability, high Q value, low loss, high out-of-band suppression, etc., debugging and processing are more convenient, and can be widely used in a variety of communication devices, adapting to the trend of integration and miniaturization of communication devices.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Physical Optics Method with Near Field Equivalent Source
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, physical optics (PO) with near field equivalent source (NFES) was proposed to quickly calculate the electromagnetic (EM) characteristics of electrically large targets. The full-wave method is used to accurately simulate the antenna. The NFES of the antenna is obtained, which is brought into PO to calculate radiation problems of electrically large targets. No matter for metal targets or dielectric targets, NFES-PO can calculate accurate results while the efficiency is improved.

articleTitle: Design of high thermal conductivity and high performance bandpass filter based on HTCC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An eight-order metal cavity waveguide filter with high thermal conductivity and high performance is designed in this paper, based on the HTCC process using high-purity (99.99%) high thermal conductivity aluminum oxide material. Introducing two cross couplings, by changing the coupling intensity of the two cross coupling, the position of transmission zero is regulated, and the passband selectivity of the filter is improved. The influence of cross-coupling variation on transmission zero position is discussed, and the variation trend and thermal simulation results are given. Through simulation optimization, the designed filter achieves an insertion loss of less than 0.15 dB within the passband of 4.8-4.96 GHz, an attenuation of 22 dB at the lower out-of-band frequency of 5 MHz, and an attenuation of 47 dB at the higher out-of-band frequency of 15MHz. It is suitable for 5G communication band and has good practical application prospect.

articleTitle: Pin Assignment Optimization of BGA Packages for EMI Mitigation Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Pin assignment of ball grid array packages is a challenging engineering problem that must meet strict electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) standards. In this paper, we propose a novel pin assignment method for electromagnetic interference mitigation using deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Firstly, the pin assignment is converted to a Markov decision process that defines state, action, and reward. Then a classical dueling double deep Q network with a physics-inspired feature encoding scheme is trained to quickly optimize the pin assignment. The design case shows that the proposed DRL method only requires less than 100 episodes to find a final solution with excellent EMC performance. As a result, the proposed DRL method can aid in computer aided engineering software for intelligent packaging design.

articleTitle: A Dual-band MIMO Antenna Pair for 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band MIMO antenna pair for 5G cellphones. A compressed concave tightlyarranged antenna pair is designed with an adjunctive resonant network formed by adding capacitors to excite an additional operating mode, thereby realizing dual-band property. The resonant frequency of the additional mode can be altered by the resonant network independently. Meanwhile, neutralization lines can be used to improve the isolation of the antenna pair. The dual- band antenna pair covers a small area of 13.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 6.3 mm2$</tex> and operates in the frequency band of both 3.5 GHz and 4.85 GHz. The isolations are better than 17 dB in 3.5 GHz band and better than 19 dB in 4.85 GHz band. The proposed dual-band antenna pair might have a good application prospect in 5G terminals.

articleTitle: Broadband Absorptive-Diffusive Rasorber with Multifunctional Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposed an absorptive-diffusive Frequency Selective Rasorber (FSR) that demonstrates broadband stealth and low-profile performance. The FSR efficiently absorbs electromagnetic waves at low frequencies and diffuses them at high frequencies. It comprises a lossy layer loaded with graphene and a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) that exhibits low-frequency reflection, medium-frequency transmission, and high-frequency diffusion properties. To achieve a low-loss transmission window, an interdigital resonator is incorporated into the lossy layer. From 2.3 to 18 GHz, the co-polarization reflection of the FSR is below −10 dB. In the frequency range of 8.4 to 11.6 GHz, the insertion loss remains below 1.5 dB, realizing the fractional bandwidth of 32%.

articleTitle: A Green's Function-Based Method for Thermal Analysis of Stacked 3-D IC Packages
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a Green's function-based method is presented to obtain the temperature distribution of stacked three-dimensional integrated circuit (3-D IC) packages. The proposed approach is derived from the power blurring (PB) method, which uses a matrix convolution technique to determine the temperature distributions. The Green's functions for representing the impulse response of unit point heat source in multilayers are derived. The method of image and intrinsic error compensation are employed to resolve the discrepancies induced by edges, corners, and pyramid structure effects. The numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-mode Dual-polarized Textile Antenna for On-/Off-Body Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-mode dual-polarization wearable textile antenna with the metasurface is proposed. Specifically, the two modes include an omnidirectional left-hand circularly polarized mode for on-body communication and a directional linearly polarized mode for off-body communication. Excited by a circular patch antenna loaded with the L-shaped slot, a pair of orthogonal omnidirectional modes of the metasurface are used to realize the on-body mode. The off-body mode is realized by using a patch antenna to excite the directional mode of the metasurface. The proposed antenna operates in the 5.8 GHz ISM band. The -10dB impedance bandwidths for on-body and off-body communication modes are 6.4% (5.59-5.96 GHz) and 16.5% (5.08-6.04 GHz), respectively, with the effective axial ratio bandwidth of 6.4% (5.59-5.96 GHz) for the on-body communication mode. The port isolation exceeds 20 dB.

articleTitle: Design of Quasi-Absorptive Ultra-Wideband Bandpass Filter Based on Stub Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a design method for quasi- absorptive ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) that can achieve quasi-reflectionless at both ports is proposed. The absorptive UWB BPF consists of a reflective UWB BPF and two resistively terminated bandstop filters (BSF), which are connected on both ports of the reflective UWB BPF. Within the passband, the BSF sections are considered as open circuit due to their high input impedance, allowing energy transmission through the reflective BPF. In the stopband, the input impedance of the BSF sections match the source impedance, resulting in the absorption of energy reflected by the reflective BPF. To demonstrate the design, an absorptive UWB BPF are designed and simulated.

articleTitle: Thermal-Fluid Co-Simulation and Modelling of IGBT with Thermal Resistance Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Due to the miniaturization of power semiconductor device and the increasing power density, temperature prediction has played an important part in module reliability. In this paper, the model of an insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) module is firstly established, and junction temperature is extracted from the numerical simulation. Furthermore, the corresponding thermal resistance network is constructed by temperature curve fitting. Under various circumstances, we achieve fine agreement with finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: An Efficient Iterative Method Using Prior Initial Value for the Integrated Circuit Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient iterative method using prior initial value is proposed to accelerate the solution of integral equation. The iterative solution occupies the most time of electromagnetic simulation. Considering the current distribution at adjacent frequency points varies continuously, the calculated current can be the prior initial value for the iterative solver to reduce the convergence steps. Especially for integrated circuit (IC) simulation, because the IC structures are electrically small, the current distribution is very similar at a frequency band, so the simulation frequency belongs to low frequency for the chip. Thus, the initial current solution at a frequency point is obtained by the interpolation of the adjacent frequency points. By adopting generalized minimum residual (GMRES) algorithm with this initial value, the integral equation is efficiently solved. An IC simulation example is given to demonstrate the efficiency of this method and validate the accuracy of the results.

articleTitle: Butler Matrix Based on Dual-Mode Transmission Lines for Millimeter Wave Dual-Polarized Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-mode Butler matrix based on the air suspended line (ASL) for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) dual-polarized antenna arrays. The ASL, which can simultaneously support TEM-mode and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>-mode, is used to design 90° hybrid coupler, 0 dB crossover, phase shift, and construct the dual-mode Butler matrix with high integration and low loss. A 4×4 dual-mode Butler matrix which is operating in mm-wave band is designed. Simulation results show that the reflection coefficients of this design are better than -15 dB in the range of 26.5 to 29.5 GHz, and have stable amplitude and phase response. The proposed butler matrix has wide application potential in 5G mm-wave dual-polarized multi-beam antenna arrays.

articleTitle: A Design and Optimization Method of Bandpass Filters Based on Space Mapping Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a design and optimization method of bandpass filters based on space mapping technique. The geometric parameters of the filter are optimized by updating two models (the iteration of the coarse model and the fine model). The fine model is obtained by the electromagnetic (EM) simulation software HFSS, and this model is used to simulate the accurate frequency response of the bandpass filter. The coarse model is founded by ADS, which is based on circuit theory and used to match the response of the fine model and compare it with the ideal filter model. A traditional waveguide bandpass filter was designed and optimized to confirm this method. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the method.

articleTitle: Computation of Electromagnetic Scattering from Ice-Sea Rough Surface via FDTD
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Finite difference time domain (FDTD) method is used to calculate the electromagnetic scattering for sea rough surface with ice. The sea rough surface and ice rough surface model is established by Monte Carlo method, while the dielectric constants of seawater and sea ice by Debye model. Then Scattering from sea-ice thickness and temperature are analyzed. The numerical results show that different ice thicknesses had little effect on the Radar Cross Section (RCS); different sea ice temperatures have an effect on the RCS, and the RCS increases with the decrease of sea ice temperature. The effects of seawater and sea ice on the target RCS are also analyzed, and the numerical results show that the sea surface and ice surface generate clutter, which leads to the reduction of the RCS.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Metasurface with Continuously Adjustable Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A hybrid continuously adjustable metasurface, which possesses electromagnetic switching and continuous tuning functions, is proposed in this paper. The design consists of a coding metasurface and an active absorber loaded with PIN diodes and varactors. By adjusting the voltage of active components, the absorbing bandwidth can be dynamically controlled. The principle of phase cancellation is introduced to achieve polarization conversion at the low frequency. The simulated results show that the absorbing bandwidth can be tuned continuously between 3.63 and 12.36 GHz, and the co-polarized reflection magnitude less than −10 dB range from 1.55 to 3.77 GHz. As a result, the broadband RCS property can be obtained.

articleTitle: Detection of Breathing in Multi-Person Scenario With MIMO-FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Currently, using micro-Doppler information extracted from radar signals to estimate human breathing has become a promising solution in health-care and fire rescue. However, accurate extraction and distinction of breathing information from multiple human targets is still a difficult problem to be solved. In this paper, we propose an effective algorithm for detection of human breathing in multi-person scenarios. The proposed algorithm separates radar signal by estimating the range and angle of arrival of different human objects, and then estimates the frequency of breathing by extracting micro-Doppler features frame by frame. In this way, we can get both the position and corresponding breathing frequency of each human object in multi-person scene. Numerical simulation and real measurements with a self-designed 24GHz MIMO-FMCW radar are both provided for validating the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Scattering from Surface Ship Using Moment Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The electromagnetic scattering of targets plays a crucial role in surface target detection and localization. However, there is currently no comprehensive methodology established for underwater target electromagnetic scattering. Most researchers simplify the scattering model by approximating the target as a magnetic dipole or a cuboid, disregarding lots of detail information of the target, which potentially leads to calculation errors. Moment method was employed to solve the electromagnetic scattering between an underwater radiation antenna and a target surface ship in this paper. By utilizing modeling software and meshing software, we establish a mathematical model of the target surface ship's electromagnetic scattering, while preserving the target's relatively complete information. Conducting simulations of the model with various parameters allows us to obtain the radiation pattern of the field, the target surface ship's current distribution, and the dynamic electromagnetic scattering characteristics. Furthermore, we calculate different motion paths and obtain multi-point imaging.

articleTitle: A Fast Acquisition Algorithm Based on Two Stage Difference and Keystone Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of limited accumulation time and dynamic influence on coherent accumulation in the acquisition of very low signal-to-noise ratio(SNR) and high dynamic Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS) signals, a fast acquisition algorithm based on two stage difference combined with keystone transform is proposed. Firstly, the algorithm uses the two stage differential delay autocorrelation method to eliminate the influence of data bit jump and carrier doppler frequency, so that the correlation accumulation time is no longer limited by data bits. Secondly, the keystone transform is used to solve the problem of pseudo-code phase walk caused by high dynamic in long time accumulation. Finally, the carrier Doppler frequency is calculated by difference. The simulation results show that the algorithm can effectively solve the problem of data bit jump and dynamic influence in long time accumulation of DSSS signal in very low SNR and high dynamic scene.

articleTitle: A Physics-Informed Neural Networks Algorithm for Simulating Semiconductor Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) algorithm for simulating semiconductor devices. It is built on drift-diffusion model (DDM) framework and aiming at describing the behavior of carriers in semiconductor devices. Such algorithm is useful for the development of semiconductor devices with high performance and reliability. In our proposed PINNs algorithm, a surrogate model for coupled drift-diffusion model with artificial neural network (ANN) is built, with backpropagation algorithm used for error computation, and Adam algorithm for parameter updating. Our numerical experiments validate its accuracy as well as convergence rate. In addition, its capability for dealing with local nonlinear problems is addressed, which is a significant potential for its further extension and application.

articleTitle: An Improved Convolutional Neural Network Based on Feature Decomposition and Cumulative Learning for Ship Detection in SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Due to the presence of objects with similar back-scattering characteristics to targets in high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images of real complex scenes, traditional algorithms for ship detection which heavily rely on ocean clutter modeling are prone to high rates of false and missing alarms, presenting very limited detection capability. In this paper, we propose a novel feature decomposition and reweighting scheme to mitigate this problem, in which multi-level integrated features are decomposed into foreground and background components. By reweighting these two types of features based on cumulative learning strategy, our method can reallocate the model attention from background features to foreground features for better understanding of non-ship and ship target characteristics. Experiments on MSAR ship dataset with a F1-score of 83.75% and 60% reduction in training time shows that the proposed method achieves a better performance in detection accuracy.

articleTitle: E-band air-filled waveguide fed SIW slot antenna array for millimeter-wave radar applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 52$</tex> slot antenna array fed by the air-filled waveguide is proposed based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). The entire structure can be easily fabricated by using low-cost printed circuit board (PCB) processing. Due to the design of air-filled waveguide feed network, the transmission loss caused by the dielectric substrate can be greatly reduced. In order to achieve a low side lobe level (SLL), the amplitude distribution of the 52 radiation slots is based on Taylor synthesis, while the amplitude distribution of the 4 coupling slots between SIW and air-filled waveguide is based on Chebyshev synthesis. From the simulation results, the impedance bandwidth of|S11|<-10dB is 4.5GHz (79 GHz ~ 83.5GHz). The maximum gain of this antenna array reaches 25.18dBi and the radiation efficiency reaches 67%. The SLL is below −20 dB in H-plane (xoz-plane) and below −24 dB in E-plane (yoz-plane), respectively. The proposed antenna array has the characteristics of high gain, low SLL and large bandwidth, which can be a candidate for the E- band millimeter-wave (MMW) radar applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Properties of High-Speed Moving Targets Coated with Non-Uniform Plasma
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the model of moving dispersion medium is established based on the Lorentz transformation Finite-Different Time-Domain (Lorentz-FDTD) method for investigated the EM properties of high-speed moving targets coated with plasma sheath. The effect of different non-uniform distribution conditions of the plasma on the electromagnetic (EM) scattering characteristics of high-speed moving targets is considered. The results shows that the different distribution of the plasma sheath affects significantly the backward EM scattering from the target when the target is in high velocity.

articleTitle: An Efficient FDTD Conformal Grid Mesh Method Based on Ray Tracing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an FDTD (finite-difference time-domain) Grid Mesh method that utilizes a ray tracing algorithm to address issues with geometrical model preprocessing. In the ray tracing algorithm, rays are directed towards objects in three directions: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x-, y-{}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z-{}$</tex>, respectively. The intersections between the ray and the object surface modeled in triangular form is obtained by solving both the triangular surface and ray equations. The state in which rays enter and exit an object is determined by the angle between the ray and the vector of the object's triangular surface. Then, the object can be evenly divided into grids. In addition, the conformal geometrical information for the partially filled meshes near the object surface has also been recorded and further used to reduce the staircase errors of the traditional FDTD method when processing the curved surface of the PEC model.

articleTitle: A Development in Imaging: Utilizing Time-Varying Orbital Angular Momentum for Noise Robustness
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The traditional vortex wave imaging method performs poorly in high-noise environments due to pulsed emission and reception of independent modes for imaging. We propose an improved imaging method employing time-varying orbital angular momentum (OAM) to enhance imaging quality. The new method could significantly improve noise robustness by generating a linear mode-modulation OAM wave within a time range. Simulation results suggest that the proposed method is effective in environments with low signal-to-noise ratios, making it a promising alternative for high-noise conditions.

articleTitle: A Double Layer Coupled Broadband Absorbing Metamaterial with Optical Transparency Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an optical transparent Metamaterial with low profile and broadband microwave absorption. The X band broadband microwave absorption is realized by designing a ring indium tin oxide (ITO) resonant unit. Furthermore, through asymmetric optimization design of a double-layer structure, ultra-wideband microwave absorption between 5.2 GHz and 18 GHz was achieved. The most crucial thing is that the overall thickness of the structure is only 6 mm, and the selected materials all have good optical transparent properties.

articleTitle: Study on differential scattering field characteristics between soil surface and semi-buried target
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, exponential distributed rough surface and Monte Carlo method are used to simulate the soil surface. Wang and Schmugge's four-component model is used to represent the dielectric properties of the soil. Based on the differential scattering field theory, the finite difference time domain method is used to study the composite electromagnetic scattering characteristics of the soil surface and semi-buried targets, and the frequency response curve of the differential radar scattering coefficient is obtained.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Modeling of Landau Damping by Fourier Neural Operator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The development of machine learning techniques enables us to discover partial differential equations from sparse data, which has important implications for modeling complex physical systems. In this paper, based on the output from 1D Vlasov-Ampere simulations, we adopt Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) to learn partial differential equations from kinetic simulation data. The trained FNO is able to predict the heat flux, in agreement with the true value from kinetic simulations. We compare the predicted physical quantities between the FNO and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) architectures, and found that the results of FNO are significantly better than that of MLP.

articleTitle: Efficient CDI-FDTD Method for Modelling Graphene-Based Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for calculating graphene-based structures in the complying divergence implicit finite-difference time-domain (CDI-FDTD) method. To begin, the differential iteration formula of graphene structure in the CDI-FDTD method is derived utilizing the auxiliary-differential-equation (ADE) method. Next, the transmission characteristics of an infinite graphene sheet in an open space are investigated by conducting simulation analyses within the CDI-FDTD framework, considering various magnetostatic or electrostatic biases. Finally, the simulation results were compared with analytical solutions and the results obtained from traditional FDTD methods, confirming the unconditional stability and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: QRCS Simulation of Equivalent Multi-Atom Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the QRCS of the equivalent multiatom physical model with additional random phase of [0,2pi] for each photon scattering process is proposed. Firstly, the interaction model between photons and atoms is established. Secondly, the QRCS results of different physical models of the equivalent multi-atom target, including one-dimensional linear target, two-dimensional planar target and three-dimensional cube target are derived. The influence of the shapes on QRCS is analyzed. The results show that when the additional random phase follows the uniformly distribution of [0,2 pi], the QRCS values of different models are almost the same at different angles. Finally, the proposed method is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Design of a Tri-Band Circularly Polarized Antenna for BeiDou and S-Band Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a tri-band circularly polarized (CP) antenna for BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) and S-band satellite communication. The proposed antenna operates at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2185\ \text{MHz}\pm 15\ \text{MHz}$</tex> with RHCP, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1995\ \text{MHz}\pm 15\ \text{MHz}$</tex> with LHCP, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1268\ \text{MHz}\pm 10\ \text{MHz}$</tex> with RHCP. All of these three antennas are dual-fed for lower axial ratio. In order to obtain better isolation, independent feeding networks are designed for each band. High dielectric constant dielectric substrate is adopted for miniaturization. The overall size of the proposed antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$48\text{mm}\times 48\text{mm}\times 9.6\text{mm}\ (0.2 \lambda\times 0.2 \lambda\times 0.04\lambda)$</tex>. Details of design, simulated results of this CP are presented and discussed. The simulated and measured results meet the requirement of BDS and satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: Half-Width Microstrip Bidirectional Leaky-Wave Antenna with Dual-Frequency High-Gain Omnidirectional Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, a design method of a dual-frequency high-gain omnidirectional antenna is investigated and implemented. The antenna is based on the bidirectional leaky-wave antenna (Bi-LWA) theory, which can generate the desired high-gain radiation at broadside in one plane. To realize omnidirectional radiation in the other plane, the half-width microstrip line (HWMSL) was utilized. Moreover, the first and second modes of the HWMSL are both employed, this leads to the antenna operated at two separated frequencies. It is thereafter revealed that a hybrid first and second mode wave will be excited at the higher operation frequency, which is due to the high-pass property of the first mode. After that, a pin-loaded method is developed to suppress the undesired mode. The antenna is finally fabricated and measured. And the simulations and measurements both show that the predicted dual-frequency high-gain omnidirectional radiations are realized.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile and Broadband Reflectarray Antenna Based on the Actual Radiation Information of Feed
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile and broadband reflectarray antenna is designed according to the actual radiation information of feed. The focal length (F) and aperture (D) of the antenna are 30 mm, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$115\ \text{mm}\times 115$</tex> mm, respectively (F/D is 0.24). The results shows that the proposed dual-bema antenna has a high gain, narrow half-power beamwidth, and wide 3 dB gain bandwidth of 24.24% (14.5-18.5 GHz).

articleTitle: Study of Evaporation Duct Height Based on Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm and RBF Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Evaporation duct is a special atmospheric stratification that frequently appears on the sea surface, which causes over the horizon propagation of electromagnetic wave and electromagnetic blind zone. Accurately and effectively predicting the evaporation duct height (EDH) has important significance for radar detection and over-the-horizon communication on the sea surface. However, traditional methods for inversing EDH has the problems of difficult model building, slow inversion calculation speed and strong dependence on inversion data source. In this paper, the propagation loss data is firstly calculated through the parabolic equation (PE) method. The radial basis function (RBF) method is applied to inverse the EDH. And then the inversion model of RBF neural network based on adaptive particle swarm optimization (APSO) is established. Comparing with the prediction results of traditional RBF and back propagation (BP) algorithm, the predicted value of APSO-RBF model for inversing EDH is consistent with the actual value, and the root-mean-square deviation (RMSE) is very smaller. Moreover, the APSO-RBF proposed in this paper has higher prediction accuracy and lower time consumption, and the overall performance is improved.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Quad-Mode Crossed-Dipole Antenna by Using Resonant Modal Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A quad-mode wideband crossed-dipole antenna is proposed and designed with the resonant modal theory (RMT). The resonant current modes for the antenna consisting of a cross and two parasitic stripes are first determined by RMT. Input terminal is then introduced and positioned at the maximum of the current modes to excite the corresponding field patterns, and, a wideband quad-mode crossed-dipole is obtained, which achieves 49.1% fractional bandwidth at −10 dB of the reflection coefficient and an overall size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.62\lambda_{0}\times 0.51\lambda_{0}\times 0.03\lambda_{0}(\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength at the center frequency).

Author Keywords: difference of stored electromagnetic field energies

articleTitle: Intelligent Classification of Spatial Targets Based on RCS Sequences
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Using the radar cross section (RCS) sequence of spatial moving targets with different azimuth, elevation angles, and poses, classification of spatial targets are achieved according to their two-dimensional images by deep residual networks. The numerical results show that the two-dimensional radar images can contain sufficient information of the spatial targets and thus exploited by the deep residual networks to achieve good classification.

articleTitle: A Simplified Model and Calculation Method for Low-Frequency and Near-Field Electromagnetic Scattering from Underwater Complex Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The study of low-frequency and Near-field electromagnetic scattering for complex underwater targets has high theoretical and engineering application potential in the field of underwater target detection. Currently, methods for electromagnetic scattering of complex targets are focused on high-frequency methods, and there are relatively few studies on electromagnetic scattering of complex underwater targets, and so far, there is no set of methods that can accurately and efficiently calculate the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of complex models. To address this issue, this paper first accurately calculates the electromagnetic scattering field of moving targets based on the moment method, which can well characterize the structural characteristics of complex underwater targets. Based on this, by approximating the target model to a more regular geometry for high-order approximation and reducing the spatial complexity, the method ensures accurate characteristics while greatly reducing the computational complexity. Simulation results confirm the feasibility and effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Combination of the Endfire Antenna and Backfire Antenna for Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a new method to designing high-gain antennas by adding dielectric substrate above and below the traditional crossover stripline endfire antenna with phase reversal, resulting in a high-gain endfire antenna and a backfire antenna. When the endfire antenna and backfire antenna are placed in a line and excited simultaneously, gain superposition in the same direction can be achieved, resulting in a high gain increase in the 9.85-10.30 GHz frequency band. The combination of two antennas achieves the highest gain of 17.63 dBi at 10.25 GHz, which is 3 dB higher than the gain of a single antenna. Therefore, the combination of endfire and backfire antennas is an effective strategy for achieving high gain improvement.

articleTitle: A High Isolation Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna Array with Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a parasitic structure is proposed to mitigate the mutual coupling among the dual-polarized base station antennas. The proposed parasitic structure is integrated into a 5-element array antenna, utilizing a staggered arrangement of antenna elements. By strategically incorporating the parasitic elements, significant enhancements in isolations of both co-polarization and cross-polarization have been achieved within the operating frequency range of 3.4-3.8 GHz. Additionally, the radiation performance of the antenna has been substantially enhanced.

articleTitle: Imaging the Partially Melt Rock System of Gonghe Basin, Qinghai, China, with Magnetotellurics in Three Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A three-dimensional (3-D) electrical resistivity model of Gonghe Basin in northeastern Tibetan plateau, unveils a complex subsurface filled with zones of partial melt, sedimentary mantles, cold plutons, and regional faults. Between the years of 2018 to 2022, 1350 broadband magnetotelluric stations were collected in an array around Gonghe Basin from which a 3-D electrical resistivity model was created with a resolvable depth of 50 km. Our resistivity model reveals a significant feature of step discontinuities between high and low resistivity blocks at different depths in the upper and middle crust. Our 3D resistivity model also shows a large higher resistivity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30-200\varOmega.m$</tex>) body at depths of 3–10 km located beneath the hot springs around the Basin. We explain that this anomaly, which is smaller than the normal resistivity range of intact granite, is mainly influenced by the high temperature environment. The most electrical resistivity robust features are two huge conductive bodies (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-10\varOmega.m$</tex>) that underlie the northeast and southern margin of Gonghe Basin below 10 km depth. The preferred electrical resistivity model suggests that the source reservoir is a narrow northeast-southwest elongated body which like a goldfish 10∼30 km below the middle basin and a vertical conductive channel in the depth could reach to 7 km below dalianhai country. Below the southern part of the basin, there is a larger high conductor that does not merge into one more diffusive and broad anomaly for a range of 1 0-40 km. Combined with the analysis of s-wave low-velocity, we believe that the most important heat source could be a zone of 5-10% partial melt in the crust.

articleTitle: A Vertically-Polarized End-Fire Leaky Wave Antenna with High Gain and Improved Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a recently proposed end-fire leaky wave antenna (LWA) with high radiation gain and efficiency under vertical polarization. By periodically loading a series of shorting-pins in the double-sided-parallel-strip-line (DSPSL), a leakage region as well as end-fire radiation condition point can be generated on the fundamental mode of transmission line with normalized phase constant equal to 1. In order to enhance the radiation efficiency of the pin-loaded LWA, the U-shaped slots are etched at the vicinity of pins on the two surfaces of DSPSL to enlarge the attenuation constant values in the end-fire operation frequency range. Hence, the high end-fire gain with high efficiency can be realized on a compact structure with a limited antenna length. A prototype is designed in final, where the good agreement between simulated and measured results confirms the predicted performances of the proposed end-fire LWA.

articleTitle: Modeling of Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on Optuna-MBNN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The Optuna-MBNN combines a multi-branch neural network (MBNN) with the Optuna optimization algorithm to overcome limitations in modeling the complex parameters of circularly polarized microstrip antennas. By utilizing the branch structure of MBNN and conducting multi parameter optimization, accurate predictions are achieved for the axial ratio, S-parameter, and gain. The Optuna framework further enhances accuracy by optimizing the network structure and hyperparameters. Experimental results demonstrate the model's high accuracy, with a mean absolute error (MAE) below 0.29.

articleTitle: Feature and EM Sensitivity Co-Assisted Method for Four-Pole Waveguide Filter Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In the electromagnetic (EM) optimization algorithm experiment, it isn't easy to optimize the sample points far away from the optimization target. In order to solve this problem, this paper combines the neuro-transfer function (neuro-TF) and sensitivity information of the sample. This paper simulates the output of microwave devices at high frequencies by building surrogate models. Sensitivity information can improve the accuracy and robustness of surrogate models. This method enables the feature model to ensure a certain accuracy under poor conditions.

articleTitle: Triple-Band Shared-Aperture Antenna with Frequency Selection Characteristics for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A triple-band Shared Aperture Antenna for base station applications is proposed, antenna operates in the frequency range of 0.63-0.95 GHz (LB), 1.6-1.76 GHz (MB), and 2.31-2.79 GHz (HB). The antenna element operating in the low-band frequency range of 0.62-0.95 GHz is positioned on a dual-band stacked antenna array, which operates at 1.35-1.83 GHz and 2.19-2.82 GHz. The low-band antenna and the dual-band antenna array share a reflector. The low-band antenna elements are designed as frequency selective surfaces (FSS) for the M/HB band. The simulation results show that the triple-band shared aperture antenna exhibits good radiation characteristics within its operating frequency bands, the LB antenna demonstrates electromagnetic transparency characteristics in the MB and HB bands.

articleTitle: A Broadband Multi-beam Array Antenna Based on Programmable Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a broadband multi-beam programmable antenna based on 1-bit broadband programmable elements. The form of the antenna is a two-dimensional planar reflection array. The antenna has the advantages of broadband, miniaturization and beam reconfiguration. The antenna is composed of 256 1-Bit broadband coding elements, with a scale of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16 \times 16$</tex>. By changing the coding state of elements at different positions in the array, the desired multi-beam can be obtained. Through simulation, we get the radiation patterns of dual-beam, three-beam, which verifies the feasibility of the antenna.

articleTitle: Fast Synthesized Methods of Radio Frequency Filter Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In the field of radio frequency (RF) device design, an optimization method of RF filter based on neural network is proposed in this paper, which is suitable for the rapid customized design of filter under different indexes. Compared with the traditional method, this optimization method avoids the complicated and tedious traditional process of using circuit theory to construct the model topology, and trial-and-error full-wave electromagnetic simulation, which significantly simplifies the optimal design of the filter. The optimization method of the filter response is performed by use of a fourth-order split resonant rings (SRRs) filter topology model operating at Ku-band with a center frequency at 12.75 GHz, a bandwidth of 0.7 GHz, and two transmission zeros at 11.2 GHz and 14.5 GHz. Finally, the optimization results are consistent with the expected index requirements.

articleTitle: Compact Phased Array Antenna with Wide-Angle Scanning for Mobile Phones
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper describes a compact four-element and eight-element array with wide-angle scanning for mobile phones. The wide-angle scanning of the two arrays are achieved with a small element spacing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.3\lambda 0$</tex>. The neutralization lines are applied to reduce mutual decoupling between close elements to better than -14 dB. An overlapped -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 25.5-27.5 GHz is achieved in the two arrays. The beam steering range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>: 60° in the four-element array and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex> 70° in the eight-element array are achieved with a compact size, a reduced decoupling, a low gain drop, a small sidelobe level, and a moderate cross-polarization level. The proposed mm-wave arrays with the superior performance of a small array size and wide beam scanning are promising for modern mobile phones.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Textile Antenna with Gain Enhancement and Bandwidth Extension
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A dual-band circularly polarized flexible wearable antenna, which exhibits gain enhancement and axial ratio bandwidth extension in the high-frequency range, has been presented for off-body communication. The antenna operates in the 3.5 GHz WiMAX band and the 5 GHz WBAN band. The antenna achieves dual-band operation by exciting two pairs of odd modes, TM10/TM01 and TM30/TM03. In order to expand the axial ratio bandwidth at high frequencies, a pair of circular arc-shaped parasitic patches are loaded. Meanwhile, a metasurface structure loaded on the top of the patch antenna can be equivalently seen as a high permittivity layer to enhance the gain at high frequencies. The proposed dual-band circularly polarized antenna has a −10dB impedance bandwidth of 9.4% (3.25-3.58GHz) and 30% (4.91-6.58GHz) respectively, with an axial ratio bandwidth of 2% (3.34-3.41GHz) and 9.3% (5.52-6.03GHz), and a peak gain of 7.2dBi and 9.7dBi, respectively. The proposed antenna is made of flexible textile material and exhibits a low SAR value, making it suitable for human body applications.

articleTitle: Spatial Correlation of the Radiation Field from the Two-dimensional Coincidence Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the spatial correlation function of a two-dimensional CIR (2D-CIR) with stochastic phase modulation is investigated. Firstly, the signal model and the coincidence imaging model based on array theory are established. Secondly, the spatial correlation function and the radiation power distribution of the reference fields are derived. Then, the relationship between the range of the modulated phase and the correlation function is analyzed. It shows that the phase modulation range of 2π is essential to ensure the performance of the 2D-CIR. Lastly, numerical simulations are conducted to validate the derivation of the correlation of the reference fields.

articleTitle: Low SidelobeLevel Transmitarray Antenna Using Hexagonal Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a linear polarization antenna with amplitude-phase independent control and using a regular hexagonal unit. The simulation result demonstrated that the sidelobes of the designed antenna effectively reduces through the Taylor amplitude distribution. Compared to antennas using square unit cell, the antenna using hexagonal unit cells the proposed antenna offers advantages of higher area utilization and lower sidelobe level.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Random Radiation Antenna Assisted by Paraboloid Cylinder Reflector
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain random radiation antenna operating within the frequency range of 22 GHz–26 GHz is proposed. The antenna comprises a random modulation radiator and a parabolic cylinder reflector. To achieve random radiation, the radiator is fed by a waveguide port. the radiation is modulated by the metasurface, which consists of 110 randomly arranged metasurface elements with different transmission phase distributions. The metasurface elements in the radiator are designed by modifying the parameters of ten distinct metasurface elements, with the phase distributions covering 360°. In order to bunch the average radiation pattern of the radiator, a parabolic cylinder reflector is proposed to achieve the high-gain radiation. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed antenna successfully achieves random radiation patterns in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x-z$</tex> plane when working in the 22-26GHz. The correlation between the radiation patterns in each sub-band is less than 0.4. Moreover, the radiation energy is concentrated within a 2° range in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y-z$</tex> plane, the S11 of the proposed antenna is less than −10dB, with the gains of the antenna being greater than 25 dB in the operating band.

articleTitle: Efficient Transient Thermal Simulation of 2.5-D Chiplet-Based Packages by Laguerre-Based Spectral-Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient approach named Laguerre-based spectral element method (LBSEM) is proposed for transient thermal analysis of 2.5-D chiplet-based packages. This algorithm is a marching-on-in-order strategy that is unconditionally stable, which uses weighted Laguerre polynomials (WLPs) as basis functions and the Galerkin testing process to eliminate the thermal field's temporal variables. In the spatial domain, the spectral element method (SEM) is employed to compute Laguerre coefficients. The efficiency and accuracy of the proposed approach are verified by analyzing transient heat behavior of a typical 2.5-D chiplet package.

articleTitle: A Wideband Series-Fed Grid-Slotted Patch Antenna with Differential Feeding
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A low-profile, single-layer, series-fed (SF) grid-slotted patch antenna with differential feeding is presented. The proposed antenna utilizes a novel cross-shaped grid-slotted patch as radiation structure. A rectangular microstrip line terminated with two tapered microstrip lines is utilized to excited the grid-slotted patch by proximity coupling. To achieve boresight radiation across the operating bandwidth, two ports of the proposed antenna are fed differentially. Simulated results show that the antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth (IMBW) of 4.93-5.99 GHz (1.06 GHz, 19.4%). In addition, the antenna is capable of maintaining good boresight radiation over the operating bandwidth, while achieving a high antenna efficiency of over 73.5%

articleTitle: An Absorptive Common-Mode Stripline Filter for High-Speed Digital Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an absorptive common-mode stripline filter, which consists of two reflective common-mode filter (CMF) units and one absorptive CMF unit. For differential-mode (DM) signal, the filter is equivalent to an all-pass filter, while for common-mode (CM) signal, it exhibits band-stop characteristics. The filter can achieve more than 90% energy absorption for CM signal in the frequency range from 4.84 GHz to 6.11 GHz, while the DM signal could pass through from DC to 10.32 GHz.

articleTitle: A Dual-Layer Ultra-Wideband Frequency Selective Surface for Electromagnetic Field Shielding
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel dual-layer frequency selective surface (FSS) is proposed for electromagnetic shielding in an ultra-wideband (UWB). The full-wave simulated results show that the proposed FSS structure has a very large stop-band with transmittance lower than −10 dB spanning from 1.89 GHz to 15.95 GHz (relative bandwidth is 157.6%), and has good angular stability and polarization insensitivity of 60°.
